cna.title: Prime Mover <= 2.2.1 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection via Base64-Encoded Comment during Migration Search-and-Replace

descriptions.value: The Prime Mover – Backup and Migration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.2.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the migration search-and-replace routine (recursiveUnserializeReplace()). An unauthenticated attacker can store a crafted, base64-encoded serialized object in wp_comments.comment_content through the standard comment-submission endpoint (wp-comments-post.php). When an administrator subsequently performs a routine Prime Mover export or restore, the plugin base64-decodes that stored value and passes it to unserialize() with no allowed_classes restriction. A Property-Oriented Programming (POP) chain is present in the plugin's own bundled Freemius library (FS_Clone_Manager::__set → FS_Option_Manager::set_option → store() → update_option()), so no additional plugin or theme is required — the plugin ships the gadget itself.

descriptions.value: MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. From 3.12.0rc0 until 3.17.0, the scorer invoke, register, and GenAI evaluate endpoints, including unauthenticated POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke, accept serialized third-party scorer data that Scorer.model_validate_json resolves using a module-path allowlist without constraining the selected class or its constructor arguments. When optional trulens and trulens-providers-litellm packages are installed, an attacker can select mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens, choose a model URI outside MLflow's native provider registry so execution uses the LiteLLM fallback, and supply api_base and api_key values that cause the server to send an outbound request to an attacker-chosen or internal host with attacker-controlled headers and body. descriptions.value: Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) is an open standard for machine learning interoperability. Prior to 1.22.0, RNNShapeInference_opset1_to_6() processes malformed RNN and LSTM nodes from opsets 1 through 6 and GRU nodes from opsets 3 through 6 without verifying that the first input has rank three. The function accesses dim(0) and dim(1) on an undersized protobuf shape, which can read outside the intended repeated field and terminate an application when onnx.shape_inference.infer_shapes() processes an untrusted model that can pass onnx.checker.check_model(). This issue is fixed in version 1.22.0.

cna.title: zip: Unbounded Symlink-Target Handling Can Abort Or Exhaust Memory During Extraction

descriptions.value: zip is a zip library for Rust that supports reading and writing simple ZIP files. From 1.3.0 until 9.0.0, ZipArchive::extract in src/read/mod.rs calls Vec::with_capacity for a symbolic link target using the attacker-controlled ZIP64 uncompressed_size before reading entry data. A small archive can request an impossible capacity, causing the infallible allocation path to abort the process before the entry is validated. The failure cannot be contained with catch_unwind or a worker thread, allowing repeated denial of service in archive-processing applications. This issue is fixed in version 9.0.0.

cna.title: Starlet versions from 0.20 before 0.33 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via regular expression backtracking when decoding chunked request bodies

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starlet 0.33 or later.

descriptions.value:
Starlet versions from 0.20 before 0.33 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via regular expression backtracking when decoding chunked request bodies.

A chunk-size line is matched as a run of hex digits, then .* and a CRLF. A run followed by a bare LF and then a CRLF can never match, and the engine retries the match once for each digit, so the time taken grows with the square of the run length. Nothing limits the length of the run, which can span several reads.

A remote attacker can occupy a worker for about a minute of CPU time with one 128 KiB request, before the application is called.

cna.title: Backstage catalog rules can be bypassed for URL locations using encoded path segments

descriptions.value: Backstage is an open framework for building developer portals. Prior to 3.9.2 and from 4.0.0 until 4.0.2, DefaultCatalogRulesEnforcer in @backstage/plugin-catalog-backend compares the raw location.target URL against catalog.rules, while URL readers canonicalize the same URL before fetching it. An authenticated user with catalog.location.create permission can use percent-encoded path segments to make an untrusted URL match a trusted location pattern even though the canonical URL resolves outside that scope. This admits entity content from an untrusted source as trusted, while further downstream consequences depend on deployment configuration. This issue is fixed in versions 3.9.2 and 4.0.2.

cna.title: Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starlet 0.33 or later.

descriptions.value:
Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory.

The request body is read in a loop that asks sysread for all of the remaining declared length at once. Perl grows the read buffer to that size before any data arrives, so a length larger than available memory makes the worker exit with an uncatchable out of memory error before the application is called.

A remote attacker can force a worker restart with each request of a few bytes.

descriptions.value: Oversized Serialized Data Payloads

solutions.value: Upgrade APM Server versions 8.3.0 through 8.19.23 to 8.19.24.
Upgrade APM Server versions 9.0.0 through 9.4.8 to 9.4.9.
Upgrade APM Server versions 9.5.0 through 9.5.5 to 9.5.6.

workarounds.value: There are no workarounds for this vulnerability.

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in APM Server can lead to denial of service via Oversized Serialized Data Payloads (CAPEC-231). An attacker who can send OpenTelemetry (OTLP) data to APM Server over HTTP can cause APM Server to exhaust its memory and terminate. This stops the intake of APM and OpenTelemetry data until APM Server restarts.

The issue is resolved in version 8.19.24, 9.4.9 and 9.5.6. The fixed versions reject OTLP/HTTP requests with a body larger than 64 MiB after decompression, as recommended by the OTLP specification.

cna.title: Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution

descriptions.value: CAPEC-586 Object Injection

Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.

Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or php_serialize session serializer. If the same session is later read with the php serializer, because session.serialize_handler is changed at runtime or differs between applications sharing a session store, bytes inside the key can be passed to the unserializer. A remote attacker able to submit a multipart upload can inject objects, which may lead to code execution when the reading application contains a suitable gadget chain, or to session corruption or denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted words domish XML Element Stream via an Unbounded Element Tree

descriptions.value: Twisted is an event-based framework for internet applications, supporting Python 3.6+. Prior to 26.10.0rc1, the twisted.words.xish.domish ExpatElementStream parser allows an unauthenticated remote peer to keep a container element open while continuously adding child elements. The parser retains the unfinished stanza as an in-memory tree without a byte or element-count limit, and XMPP pre-authentication stream parsing exposes this behavior before credentials are accepted. A single connection can therefore exhaust server memory and terminate the process. This issue is fixed in version 26.10.0rc1.

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in the HTTP/2 request body reader of mtrudel bandit allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to hold stream processes open indefinitely via WINDOW_UPDATE or empty SETTINGS frames sent while a Plug reads the request body.

Bandit.HTTP2.Stream.do_read_data/4 in lib/bandit/http2/stream.ex waits for each frame with a fresh read_timeout. A stream WINDOW_UPDATE, or the zero-delta window update that every empty SETTINGS frame delivers to all streams, ends the wait without delivering any body data, and the loop starts a new full countdown. A client that sends one of these 9-byte frames before each countdown expires keeps read_body blocked, together with the stream process and whatever the application holds while reading, for as long as it likes.

This issue affects bandit: from 1.4.0 before 1.14.0.

4. The stream stays open for 120 s, eight times the default 15 s `read_timeout`. Without the WINDOW_UPDATE frames, the server ends the read after about 15 s.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Per-receive timeout. Bandit.HTTP2.Stream.read_data/2 passes a flat read_timeout (default 15,000 ms) to do_read_data/4, which blocks in do_recv/2's receive ... after timeout.

2. Non-progress frames end the wait. A stream WINDOW_UPDATE, delivered through Bandit.HTTP2.Connection.handle_frame/3, or an empty SETTINGS frame, which delivers a zero-delta window update to every stream, is matched inside that receive. do_recv_send_window_update/2 returns a bare %Stream{}, and do_read_data/4 recurses with the identical timeout, restarting the countdown.

3. Nothing else bounds the read. The transport read timeout fires only when no bytes arrive, max_bytes is decremented only by DATA frames, and neither WINDOW_UPDATE nor SETTINGS frames are rate limited. The send path in do_send_data/4 uses a progress-based deadline; the read path does not.

cna.title: WHIZZ <= 1.1.8 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary User Password Reset

descriptions.value: The WHIZZ WordPress plugin through 1.1.8 does not validate the password-reset key before updating a user's password, relying only on a nonce that is exposed to unauthenticated visitors, allowing attackers to set an arbitrary password for any user, including administrators, and fully take over their accounts.

cna.title: Path traversal in post media lets any registered user read server files

descriptions.value: Where the Discord provider is configured, any registered user can read any regular file the publishing worker can read and have it delivered byte for byte to a Discord server they control.

Files within reach include those that hold the JWT signing secret, the database address and provider client secrets, such as the instance's environment file, mounted secret files and application logs, and the worker's process environment.

A second route lets a user with a connected Dribbble, TikTok or Pinterest channel learn whether a path exists and whether it is a file or a directory, and exhaust the backend's memory with one request by pointing at a device file, which stops the backend from answering any organization until it is killed.
A third route, on instances using local storage with an empty cloud bucket URL, reaches the same file read without needing a WordPress site.

exploits.value: Exploitation was demonstrated end to end against unmodified builds of the backend and the orchestrator at commit 3a7d28b7ad96, using only a self-registered account: a file outside the upload directory arrived byte for byte as an attachment in the attacker's Discord channel. The validation-time route and the stored media route were also exercised separately against the same builds.

timeline.value: Anthropic has disclosed a thorough report of this vulnerability including a working PoC to Postiz
Postiz has reproduced the vulnerability and is working on a fix
Postiz has pushed a fix for this vulnerability and verified it
Postiz has created a release and published the advisory

workarounds.value: Set DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true. The attacker needs an ordinary account, so closing self-registration limits exposure to people who already hold one. This reduces reach, it does not close the issue.
If you do not need the Discord provider, leave its client id, client secret and bot token unset. This removes the main route only; the other routes remain.

descriptions.value:
When a post is published, Postiz treats a media path that is not a web address as a file on the server's disk, but it does not check that the file lies inside the upload directory. A registered user can store a crafted media path with a post, get it past the checks that normally restrict it, and have the publishing worker read an arbitrary file and send it as an attachment to a Discord server the user controls.

The same unconfined reads can be reached through two further routes. One tells the caller whether a file exists and can exhaust the backend's memory, the other delivers the file the same way as the main route. Self-registration is open by default, so the attacker needs no existing account.

configurations.value: The main route requires the Discord provider to be enabled, that is DISCORD_CLIENT_ID, DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET and DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_ID set. These are empty in the shipped docker-compose.yaml. The storage provider does not matter.
The validation-time route requires a Dribbble, TikTok or Pinterest provider to be configured.
The shipped container runs the worker as root, so every file root can read is exposed. Self-registration is open unless DISABLE_REGISTRATION is set to true.

cna.title: Twisted: Denial of Service in the Twisted IMAP4 Server via a Negative Literal Size in SEARCH

descriptions.value: Twisted is an event-based framework for internet applications, supporting Python 3.6+. Prior to 26.10.0rc1, twisted.mail.imap4.IMAP4Server reaches twisted.mail.imap4.parseNestedParens with a negative literal size in an authenticated SEARCH command after the client enters the selected mailbox state. The negative size moves the parser cursor below zero, and Python's negative indexing prevents the synchronous scanning loop from terminating. The loop freezes the single-threaded reactor, stopping other IMAP connections and any SMTP or POP3 services hosted in the same process until restart. This issue is fixed in version 26.10.0rc1.

cna.title: graphql-scalars PhoneNumber scalar is vulnerable to regular expression denial of service

descriptions.value: GraphQL Scalars is a library of custom GraphQL scalars for creating precise type-safe GraphQL schemas. From 1.24.1 until 2.0.1, GraphQLPhoneNumber in src/scalars/PhoneNumber.ts uses ambiguous nested digit quantifiers that backtrack exponentially when a PhoneNumber value contains a run of digits followed by a character that makes the match fail. GraphQL evaluates parseLiteral during document validation and parseValue during variable coercion before resolver authentication or authorization, so a small unauthenticated request can block the Node.js event loop and stall the server process. serialize is also affected when unvalidated stored values are returned through the scalar. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.1.

cna.title: Serialize JavaScript: Cross-site scripting (XSS) via unescaped </script at the end of a serialized function body

descriptions.value: Serialize JavaScript serializes JavaScript values to a superset of JSON that includes regular expressions and functions. Prior to 7.1.3, the function-source escaping logic does not neutralize a bare closing-script prefix when attacker-influenced function source text ends exactly at that prefix. Because each function body is escaped independently, a delimiter supplied by surrounding serialized output can terminate an HTML script element, and a later serialized value supplies injected markup that becomes a live element in the page. Exploitation requires control of a serialized function's source text, such as through a spoofed toString(). This issue is fixed in version 7.1.3.

cna.title: vLLM: Out-of-vocabulary prompt token id passes input validation and triggers a CUDA device-side assert (engine crash / DoS)

descriptions.value: vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, vllm/tokenizers/hf.py computes max_token_id with an off-by-one upper bound, allowing a pre-tokenized prompt ID equal to the vocabulary size to pass validation. For a tensor-parallel size of one and an exact multiple-of-64 vocabulary, VocabParallelEmbedding.forward does not mask that value before F.embedding uses it, causing a CUDA device-side assertion and terminating the engine. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

descriptions.description: CWE-129: Improper Validation of Array Index

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenCATS before 0.12.0 Stored XSS via MRU Navigation Panel

descriptions.value: OpenCATS before 0.12.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows a low-privileged authenticated user to inject HTML/JavaScript payloads by setting a Candidate, Company, Contact, Job Order, or List name/title field, which is stored unsanitized and later rendered unescaped in the 'Recent' (MRU) navigation panel displayed on nearly every page via lib/MRU.php's getFormatted() function. Attackers can exploit this by crafting a malicious record name that executes arbitrary JavaScript in the session of any other user, including Site Administrators, who views the record, enabling session/cookie theft and privilege escalation to full administrative control.

cna.title: Wasmtime: Panic lowering a host-created component model stream into a guest that expects a different payload type

descriptions.value: Wasmtime is a runtime for WebAssembly. From 46.0.0 until 48.0.7 and 49.0.4, lowering a host-created component-model stream or future into a guest can omit a required payload-type check after the value passes through guest code and returns through StreamAny, FutureAny, Val::Stream, Val::Future, or an equivalent typed reader. A malicious guest that controls exported function types or returned values can cause the host to pass the type-erased value to a guest expecting a different payload type, which panics the Wasmtime host. This issue is fixed in versions 48.0.7 and 49.0.4.

cna.title: go-guerrilla crashes on a bare XCLIENT command (7-byte slice off-by-one panic)

descriptions.description: CWE-129: Improper Validation of Array Index

descriptions.value: Go-Guerrilla SMTP Daemon is a lightweight SMTP server written in Go. In 1.6.7 and earlier, according to the repository advisory's structured affected range, server.go defines the seven-byte cmdXCLIENT token, but the XCLIENT handler slices input[8:] after matching only that seven-byte verb, so a bare command causes an out-of-bounds panic in handleClient and terminates the daemon because that connection goroutine does not recover the panic. The issue is reachable by an unauthenticated client when the non-default xclient_on setting is enabled; no HELO command is required. The repository fix is present in version 1.6.7-1.

cna.title: zip: Arbitrary file write outside the extraction directory, because ZipArchive::extract validates symlink targets lexically. (The defense against CVE-2025-29787 was broken in v7.2.0)

descriptions.value: zip is a zip library for Rust that supports reading and writing simple ZIP files. From 7.2.0 until 9.0.0, ZipArchive::extract and ZipArchive::extract_unwrapped_root_dir use safe_prepare_path in src/read/zipfile.rs and simplified_components in src/path.rs to validate symbolic link targets with a lexical prefix comparison rather than resolving each intermediate link. An attacker who knows or can guess the absolute extraction destination can create a chain whose apparent target remains under the destination while an intermediate symlink resolves outside it, allowing attacker-controlled files to be created or overwritten with the extracting process's privileges. On Windows, discarded drive and UNC prefixes can permit a single-link escape when the process has SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege, such as through administrator rights or Developer Mode. This regression is distinct from CVE-2025-29787. This issue is fixed in version 9.0.0.

cna.title: Unrestricted network access between execution contexts in KNIME Business Hub

descriptions.value: CAPEC-180 Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels
CAPEC-300 Port Scanning

Unrestricted network access between execution contexts in KNIME Business Hub before version 1.19.0 allows an authenticated remote user to access open network ports on executors in different execution contexts. This only poses a security issue if the IP address of the attacked executor is know and there are open network ports that provided access without further authentication. By default no network ports are open. However, depending on the running workflows, ports may be opened and provide an attack surface. As a workaround, network policies can be created manually.

descriptions.value: The Recipe Card Blocks Lite WordPress plugin before 3.6.4 does not perform an authorization check before rendering posts through its recipe print feature, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the title, ID and recipe content of unpublished posts, including drafts, pending, private and password-protected posts, that contain a recipe card block. cna.title: zip: AES Entry HMAC Authentication Bypass on Premature EOF

descriptions.value: zip is a zip library for Rust that supports reading and writing simple ZIP files. From 0.6.0 until 9.0.0, the AES entry reader in src/aes.rs verifies its HMAC only when the attacker-controlled data counter reaches zero. If the underlying bounded reader reaches the real end of the archive while data_remaining is still positive, or if an encrypted entry has no payload, the reader can return a clean end of stream without reading and comparing the authentication tag. Applications using by_index_decrypt, by_name_decrypt, by_path_decrypt, or password-enabled by_index_with_options can therefore accept modified plaintext without an authentication error. This issue is fixed in version 9.0.0.

cna.title: baserCMS: BcCustomContent file fields can be configured to allow executable file extensions such as php, leading to arbitrary PHP file upload

descriptions.value: baserCMS is a website development framework. Starting in version 5.0.0-beta1 and prior to versions 5.3.2 and 5.4.2, `PermissionGroupsService::build()` reads a plugin's `config/permission.php` to decide what each user group may reach. When that file is absent it writes a wildcard allow rule instead: `url` `/baser/<prefix>/<plugin>/*`, `method` `*`, `auth` true, for every non-admin group. BcCustomContent has no such file in any release. After an administrator installs it, the default `operators` group can store and execute arbitrary PHP under the document root. Versions 5.3.2 and 5.4.2 patch the issue.

cna.title: Forged signed tokens let any registered user take over other users and organizations

descriptions.value: A registered user can obtain a validly signed token with claims of their choosing and use it as a login session for another user, without knowing any identifier of the victim when database filter objects are used as claims.

An attacker can join any other organization as super administrator, using an organization id that is exposed by any shared post preview link, read its API key and channel list and schedule posts through its connected social accounts.
An attacker can reset the password of a user whose id they know, and can obtain an organization with a lifetime top-tier subscription through the enterprise provisioning endpoint.
Forged tokens do not expire and cannot be told apart from genuine ones.
The narrower invitation route lets a user who may invite team members repeatedly stop the scheduled posts of a channel of another organization, and lift the channel limit of their own plan.

exploits.value: Exploitation was demonstrated end to end against an unmodified backend build at commit 3a7d28b7ad96: a second self-registered user became super administrator of another user's organization and read its API key. Session, password reset, enterprise and subscription tokens obtained the same way were each accepted by their endpoints.

timeline.value: Anthropic has disclosed a thorough report of this vulnerability including a working PoC to Postiz
Postiz has reproduced the vulnerability and is working on a fix
Postiz has pushed a fix for this vulnerability and verified it
Postiz has created a release and published the advisory

workarounds.value: If you do not use channels that rely on the Postiz browser extension, block POST /integrations/extension-refresh at your reverse proxy. This removes the main signing route; the team invitation route remains.
Set DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true. The attacker needs an ordinary account, so closing self-registration limits exposure to people who already hold one. This reduces reach, it does not close the issue.

descriptions.value:
Postiz signs its session, invitation and password reset tokens with one shared secret and without any marker of what a token is for. A route that refreshes the credentials of a browser-extension channel signed data taken from the request itself and stored the result where the requesting user can read it back. A user could therefore obtain a validly signed token containing any claims they choose, which the application accepts as a session, as an organization invitation with a chosen role, as a password reset or as an enterprise provisioning token.

A second, narrower route that creates team invitations signs extra fields from the request body in the same way.

configurations.value: The instance must be able to reach api2.skool.com, as any instance using the Skool provider can. No setting has to be changed.

With Stripe billing configured, the attacker's own plan must allow one channel and the target organization must not be on the STANDARD tier. The session and password reset tokens are not affected by these limits.
Self-registration is open unless DISABLE_REGISTRATION is set to true.

cna.title: Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted conch Telnet Transport via an Unbounded Subnegotiation Buffer

descriptions.value: Twisted is an event-based framework for internet applications, supporting Python 3.6+. Prior to 26.10.0rc1, twisted.conch.telnet.Telnet.dataReceived appends every byte received after IAC SB to a persistent subnegotiation buffer until IAC SE is received, without applying a maximum length. Telnet option negotiation occurs before authentication, so an unauthenticated peer can omit the terminator and continuously grow the buffer. The resulting memory exhaustion can terminate the process and every service it hosts. This issue is fixed in version 26.10.0rc1.

cna.title: LangGraph: Namespace labels containing `.` reach other namespaces in Postgres and SQLite stores

descriptions.value: LangGraph checkpoint savers provide Postgres- and SQLite-backed state persistence for LangGraph workflows and agents. Prior to langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.1.3 and langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.2, PostgresStore, AsyncPostgresStore, SqliteStore, and AsyncSqliteStore flatten namespace labels with ".".join(namespace), while BaseStore validates labels only for put and aput. Unvalidated dotted labels passed through get, search, delete, list_namespaces, their asynchronous equivalents, or direct batch and abatch operations can resolve to another tenant's stored namespace, allowing cross-namespace reads, overwrites, or deletion. InMemoryStore is not affected because it compares namespace tuples. This issue is fixed in langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.1.3 and langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.2.

cna.title: baserCMS: Public Web API mail-form submission bypasses image CAPTCHA

descriptions.value: baserCMS is a website development framework. In versions 5.0.0 before 5.3.2 and 5.4.0 before 5.4.2, the public POST /baser/api/bc-mail/mail_messages/add/{mailContentId}.json endpoint accepts submissions without enforcing the form's auth_captcha setting. BcMail\Controller\Api\MailMessagesController::add() and MailMessagesService::create() omit the BcCaptchaService::check() verification of captcha_id and auth_captcha performed by MailController::submit() in the web UI. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the API can therefore automate submissions without solving the enabled image challenge. The API disables FormProtection and has no rate limit; submissions can generate administrator-inbox spam, send attacker-influenced auto-replies to third parties when an email field is present, and accumulate mail_messages database records when save_info is enabled. The API already enforces the isAccepting() check added for CVE-2026-30878; the missing CAPTCHA check is a separate control failure. This issue has been patched in versions 5.3.2 and 5.4.2.

cna.title: ML-KEM key-pair lookup can bind an unrelated or attacker-planted public key, exposing encapsulated shared secrets

descriptions.value: In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `>= 2.0.0-rc3, <= 2.0.0-rc8`, the ML-KEM key-pair lookup functions (`FindMLKEMKeyPair`, `FindMLKEMKeyPairs`, `FindMLKEMKeyPairsWithAttributes`) locate the public half of an ML-KEM key pair by `CKA_ID`/`CKA_LABEL` and never verify it against the private key. In addition, the "ID only" fallback search runs even when the private key has no `CKA_ID`, so the search template reduces to the public-key class and the ML-KEM key type and the first ML-KEM public key on the token is returned. `Encapsulate()` on the resulting key pair encrypts the fresh shared secret to that key, so its owner — not the holder of the private key the caller looked up — can recover the secret. An attacker who can open an unauthenticated session on the token and plant a public `CKK_ML_KEM` object carrying the victim's `CKA_ID`/`CKA_LABEL` receives the shared secrets for encapsulations performed through the substituted key pair, compromising the confidentiality of those secrets and of everything protected by keys derived from them. The v1 module paths have no ML-KEM support and are not affected.

descriptions.value: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions before 10.1.8, the allowedPath guard receives only the requested pathname, but the underlying send step selects the file to serve afterwards, so a request for a directory resolves to its default index file and an extensionless request resolves through the configured extensions to a matching file. The selected file is streamed without being re-checked against allowedPath, so a guard that denies a specific file is bypassed by requesting its directory or extensionless form. An unauthenticated client can read files inside the static root that the application meant to keep private whenever the denied file is reachable as a directory index or an extension match. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.8, and users should upgrade to 10.1.8 or later. As a workaround, also deny the directory and extensionless forms in allowedPath, or disable the index and extensions options.

An unauthenticated client can read files inside the static root that the application meant to keep private whenever the denied file is reachable as a directory index or an extension match. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.8, and users should upgrade to 10.1.8 or later. As a workaround, also deny the directory and extensionless forms in allowedPath, or disable the index and extensions options.

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starman 0.4019 or later.

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starman 0.4019 or later.

descriptions.value:
Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl allow a stalled request body to hold a worker indefinitely, as read_timeout covers only the headers.

Content-Length and chunked request bodies are read with blocking reads and no deadline. A client that sends complete headers and then stalls or trickles the body keeps the worker waiting until it disconnects.

A remote attacker can take every worker with a few such connections, five with the default worker count, so the server stops answering requests.

Version 0.4019 applies read_timeout to each wait for body data and adds a body_timeout limit, 300 seconds by default, on the total time to read a body.

cna.title: staging: rtl8723bs: fix OOB reads in rtw_get_wps_ie()

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

staging: rtl8723bs: fix OOB reads in rtw_get_wps_ie()

rtw_get_wps_ie() iterates over IE data from network frames without
validating that the IE header and payload fit within the remaining
buffer before reading them. Specifically:

- in_ie[cnt + 1] is read without checking cnt + 1 < in_len
- memcmp(&in_ie[cnt + 2], ...) accesses cnt + 2 without bounds check
- in_ie[cnt + 1] is used as length without verifying payload fits

Add bounds checks at the top of the loop body to break early if fewer
than 2 bytes remain for the IE header, or if the declared payload
extends past the end of the buffer. Also require at least 4 bytes of
payload before comparing the WPS OUI.

descriptions.value: hashcat contains a heap-based buffer overflow (out-of-bounds write) in the outfile_write() function in src/outfile.c. When assembling output into a fixed-size buffer (HCBUFSIZ_LARGE, ~16 MB), the function sequentially appends the username, separator, hash, and plaintext via memcpy without validating that the accumulated length stays within the buffer capacity. When run with --username --show against a crafted hash file containing an oversized username that nearly fills the buffer, the total assembled output exceeds the buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow that can corrupt memory and crash the process.

cna.title: wifi: carl9170: bound memcpy length in cmd callback to prevent OOB read

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: carl9170: bound memcpy length in cmd callback to prevent OOB read

When the firmware sends a command response with a length mismatch,
carl9170_cmd_callback() logs the mismatch and calls carl9170_restart()
but then falls through to memcpy(ar->readbuf, buffer + 4, len - 4).
Since len comes from the firmware and can exceed ar->readlen, this
copies more data than the readbuf was allocated for.

Bound the memcpy to min(len - 4, ar->readlen) so that the response
is still completed -- avoiding repeated restarts from queued garbage --
while preventing an overread past the response buffer.

cna.title: super: fix emergency thaw deadlock on frozen block devices

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

super: fix emergency thaw deadlock on frozen block devices

do_thaw_all_callback() calls bdev_thaw() while holding sb->s_umount
exclusively. If the block device was frozen via bdev_freeze() dropping
the last block layer freeze reference calls fs_bdev_thaw() which
reacquires s_umount:

  do_thaw_all_callback(sb)
    super_lock_excl(sb)                     # holds sb->s_umount
    bdev_thaw(sb->s_bdev)
      mutex_lock(&bdev->bd_fsfreeze_mutex)
      # bd_fsfreeze_count drops 1 -> 0
      bd_holder_ops->thaw == fs_bdev_thaw
        get_bdev_super(bdev)
          bdev_super_lock(bdev, true)
            super_lock(sb, true)
              down_write(&sb->s_umount)     # same task: deadlock

The emergency thaw worker deadlocks against itself holding both
s_umount and bd_fsfreeze_mutex. That fscks any subsequent unmount,
freeze, or thaw of that filesystem and block device.

bdev_super_lock() even documents the violated requirement with
lockdep_assert_not_held(&sb->s_umount).

Acquiring bd_fsfreeze_mutex under s_umount also inverts the
bd_fsfreeze_mutex vs. s_umount ordering established by
bdev_{freeze,thaw}() and can thus ABBA against a concurrent block-layer
freeze even when the recursive path isn't hit.

Fix this by not holding s_umount around the bdev_thaw() loop at all. Pin
the superblock with an active reference instead as
filesystems_freeze_callback() does. The active reference keeps the
superblock from being shut down and so ->s_bdev stays valid without
holding s_umount. The block-layer-held freeze is dropped by
fs_bdev_thaw() with FREEZE_MAY_NEST | FREEZE_HOLDER_USERSPACE exactly as
a regular unfreeze would and thaw_super_locked() handles
filesystem-level freezes as before.

The emergency thaw path has deadlocked like this in one form or
another for a long long time but the current exclusively-held
shape dates back to commit [1] where thaw_bdev() already ended in
thaw_super() with s_umount held by do_thaw_all_callback().

cna.title: libceph: fix two unsafe bare decodes in decode_lockers()

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The flaw is reached when libceph decodes a crafted MOSDOpReply for the lock.get_info class method received over the Ceph messenger TCP session from a compromised or malicious OSD; no local syscall or ioctl is required on the victim.
AC:L - A malicious OSD can deterministically send struct_len=0 or craft num_lockers so the decode pointer reaches end, triggering both bare decodes on every attempt without races, special memory layout, or rare kernel configuration.
PR:N - The attacker acts as the remote Ceph OSD peer and needs no account or privileges on the victim Linux host; any kernel RBD client connected to a multi-tenant or attacker-controlled cluster is exposed during automatic exclusive-lock operations.
UI:N - Once an RBD image is mapped, ceph_cls_lock_info() is invoked automatically during exclusive-lock acquisition and object-map lock recovery; no further victim user or administrator action is required at exploit time.
S:U - The slab out-of-bounds reads and any resulting kernel memory corruption occur entirely within the victim host kernel running the Ceph client, without crossing VM, container, or IOMMU security boundaries.
C:H - Bare ceph_decode_32/8 past the validated reply boundary perform slab out-of-bounds reads of adjacent kernel memory; the leaked u32 can drive kzalloc_objs() sizing and the OOB u8 directly controls the lock-type field consumed by RBD lock logic.
I:H - Attacker-influenced out-of-bounds values feed heap allocation sizing and lock-type discrimination in kernel lock-handling paths, providing memory-corruption primitives in a privileged parser that can be leveraged beyond simple information disclosure.
A:H - Slab out-of-bounds reads can trigger KASAN faults or kernel oops on instrumented builds, and attacker-controlled locker counts can force very large kzalloc attempts causing severe memory pressure, OOM conditions, and loss of availability on RBD client hosts.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

libceph: fix two unsafe bare decodes in decode_lockers()

decode_lockers() in cls_lock_client.c contains two bare decode operations
that allow a malicious or compromised OSD to trigger slab-out-of-bounds
reads:

1. ceph_decode_32(p) at the num_lockers field has no preceding bounds
   check. ceph_start_decoding() accepts struct_len=0 as valid -- the
   internal ceph_decode_need(p, end, 0, bad) always passes -- so when an
   OSD sends struct_len=0, ceph_start_decoding() returns success with
   p == end. The immediately following bare ceph_decode_32(p) then reads
   4 bytes past the validated buffer boundary. The garbage value is
   passed directly to kzalloc_objs() as the locker count.

   The sibling function decode_watchers() in osd_client.c already uses
   ceph_decode_32_safe() after its own ceph_start_decoding() call.
   decode_lockers() was the only site using the bare variant.

2. ceph_decode_8(p) after the decode_locker() loop has no preceding
   bounds check. If an OSD crafts num_lockers such that the loop
   advances p exactly to end, the subsequent bare ceph_decode_8(p) reads
   one byte past the validated buffer boundary. The result is passed
   directly into *type, which is used as a lock type discriminator by
   callers, giving an OSD-controlled one-byte OOB read with direct
   influence over the lock type field.

Fix both by replacing bare operations with their safe variants:
  ceph_decode_32(p) -> ceph_decode_32_safe(p, end, *num_lockers,
                                           err_inval)
  ceph_decode_8(p)  -> ceph_decode_8_safe(p, end, *type,
                                          err_free_lockers)

The goto targets differ intentionally:
  err_inval: is a new label returning -EINVAL directly. It is used for
  the pre-allocation failure path where *lockers is not yet allocated
  and must not be passed to ceph_free_lockers().

  err_free_lockers: is the existing label. It is used for the
  post-allocation failure path where *lockers is allocated and must
  be freed.

ret is set to -EINVAL before ceph_decode_8_safe() so that
err_free_lockers returns the correct error code on bounds violation.
Without this, err_free_lockers would return a stale ret value (0 from
the successful decode_locker() loop), silently swallowing the error.

-EINVAL is correct for both failure paths. The data received from the
OSD is structurally malformed. -ENOMEM would misrepresent the failure
class to callers and to stable@ backporters triaging error paths.

Attacker model: a malicious or compromised OSD in a multi-tenant Ceph
deployment can trigger this against any kernel client that issues the
lock.get_info class method (e.g. during RBD exclusive lock acquisition).

cna.title: userfaultfd: prevent registration of special VMAs

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

userfaultfd: prevent registration of special VMAs

Vova Tokarev says:

  userfaultfd allows registration on shadow stack VMAs.  With userfaultfd
  access, you can register on the shadow stack, discard a page ... and
  inject a page with chosen return addresses via UFFDIO_COPY.

Update vma_can_userfault() to reject VM_SHADOW_STACK.

While on it, also reject VM_SPECIAL so that if a driver would implement
vm_uffd_ops, it wouldn't be possible to register special VMAs with
userfaultfd.

Since VM_SPECIAL includes VM_DONTEXPAND which is set but hugetlb, exclude
hugetlb VMAs from the check for VM_SPECIAL.

cna.title: drm/xe/vf: Add drm_dev guards when detaching CCS read/write buffers

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The path is reached through the local DRM device (/dev/dri/renderD*) — GEM object creation/mmap and process teardown driving TTM BO destruction; no network or remote input is involved.
AC:L - No race must be won: a local user only needs live CCS-attached BOs when the device is unbound/hot-removed, after which every subsequent BO release deterministically walks the stale pointers, and BO lifetime is fully under the user's control.
PR:L - Only ordinary access to the render node is required to create and hold the CCS-attached buffer objects whose destruction triggers the fault; no capability check guards xe_sriov_vf_ccs_detach_bo().
UI:N - The faulting code runs automatically from the BO release path (exit_mmap/ttm_bo_release) with no action by any other user; the unbind/hot-remove event is an administrative or host-side operation, not victim interaction.
S:U - The freed objects and the resulting corruption all belong to the same kernel within the VF guest; no VM, IOMMU or sandbox boundary is crossed.
C:H - After unbind, ctx->mig_q, pool->bo/shadow and pool->cpu_addr are dangling devm-freed objects that are read (xe_mem_pool_swap_shadow_locked, xe_map_memcpy_to from pool->cpu_addr), so reallocated kernel memory can be read and its contents propagated, giving a use-after-free disclosure primitive.
I:H - The same path writes through the stale mappings — memset(cs, MI_NOOP, bb->sa_node.size), xe_map_wr into the freed LRC BO vmap and a memcpy into the freed shadow BO — so freed memory that may already be reused is overwritten, a use-after-free write primitive.
A:H - The reported and reproducible outcome is a kernel NULL pointer dereference oops in xe_sriov_vf_ccs_rw_update_bb_addr() during process exit, killing the task in kernel context and destabilizing the machine.

cna.title: Bluetooth: hci_sync: extend conn_hash lookup critical sections

scenarios.value:
AV:A - The affected code is the Bluetooth HCI sync/scan management layer; both sides of the race are driven by LE radio events (connection complete, disconnect, periodic advertising sync creation/termination) from a device in radio range, requiring no local access.
AC:L - A nearby attacker drives both sides of the race — repeated LE connect/disconnect and PA sync setup/teardown queue the hci_sync work while concurrently triggering hci_conn_del() on the event workqueue — so the window can be re-attempted arbitrarily until won.
PR:N - The vulnerable hci_update_passive_scan_sync()/hci_update_accept_list_sync()/hci_le_set_ext_scan_param_sync() paths are invoked automatically by the kernel in response to incoming LE connection and periodic-advertising events; the remote attacker needs no credentials or pairing on the target.
UI:N - No victim action is needed — background LE scanning and accept-list updates are performed autonomously by the host stack whenever connection state changes.
S:U - The use-after-free occurs in kernel memory and its impact is confined to the kernel's own security authority, with no crossing into a separate authorization scope such as a hypervisor or IOMMU boundary.
C:H - The freed hci_conn is read after release (conn->dst, conn->dst_type, PHY parameters), and a heap-groomed replacement object lets the attacker read attacker-chosen or sensitive kernel data, which can additionally be exfiltrated via the resulting accept-list/scan parameters.
I:H - hci_conn is kfree()'d via bt_link_release() while still referenced, so reallocating the slab with a controlled object yields write/control-flow primitives typical of slab use-after-free, enabling kernel memory corruption and privilege escalation.
A:H - Dereferencing the freed hci_conn readily causes slab corruption, KASAN splats, or an oops/panic in the Bluetooth workqueues, taking down the kernel.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: hci_sync: extend conn_hash lookup critical sections

Using RCU-protected pointers outside the critical sections without
refcount is incorrect and may result to UAF.

Extend critical section to cover both hci_conn_hash lookup and use of
the returned conn.

Add surrounding rcu_read_lock() also when return value is not used, in
preparation for RCU lockdep requirement to hci_lookup_le_connect().

This avoids concurrent deletion of the conn before we are done
dereferencing it.

Also, make sure to hold hdev->lock when accessing hdev->accept_list.

cna.title: media: rtl2832: fix use-after-free in rtl2832_remove()

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: rtl2832: fix use-after-free in rtl2832_remove()

cancel_delayed_work_sync() is called before i2c_mux_del_adapters()
in rtl2832_remove(). While the cancel waits for any running instance
of i2c_gate_work to finish, it does not prevent the timer from being
rescheduled by a concurrent thread.

During probe, the r820t_attach() call attempts I2C transfers through
the mux adapter. These transfers go through i2c_mux_master_xfer(),
which calls rtl2832_deselect() after the transfer completes,
rescheduling i2c_gate_work via schedule_delayed_work(). If this
transfer is still in flight when rtl2832_remove() runs,
rtl2832_deselect() can reschedule i2c_gate_work after it has been
cancelled, causing a use-after-free when kfree(dev) is called.

Fix this by calling i2c_mux_del_adapters() before
cancel_delayed_work_sync(). Once the mux adapter is unregistered, no
new I2C transfers can go through it, so rtl2832_deselect() can no
longer reschedule i2c_gate_work. The subsequent
cancel_delayed_work_sync() is then guaranteed to be final.

cna.title: smb/client: handle overlapping allocated ranges in fallocate

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The malformed input is the FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES response parsed by the SMB client from a remote peer, so a malicious, compromised, or MITM'd SMB server exploits this purely over the network (TCP/445) against the mounted client.
AC:L - The server fully and deterministically controls the returned range file_offset/length fields; a single record with bit 63 set in length reliably inflates the loop's len past the 1 MB buffer with no race, timing, or memory-layout precondition.
PR:N - The attacker is the remote SMB server (or a network MITM) and needs no account, credentials, or privileges on the victim client; only the pre-existing SMB session the client itself established is required.
UI:N - Against an already-mounted share (fstab/autofs/systemd automount) a compromised or MITM'd server needs no victim action, and fallocate/posix_fallocate is issued routinely by ordinary applications such as databases, VM images, and download managers.
S:U - The out-of-bounds read, the corrupted write offsets, and the resulting crash all stay within the kernel of the client host; no VM, IOMMU, or sandbox boundary is crossed.
C:H - Because smb3_simple_fallocate_write_range() advances buf by every 64 KB chunk written, the inflated length walks far past the 1 MB kvzalloc'd zero buffer and transmits adjacent kernel heap memory straight back to the attacker's server, yielding a large sequential kernel memory disclosure.
I:H - The negative length drives off backwards and lets attacker-chosen offsets be zero-filled over ranges of the victim's file that hold real data, and the original defect makes fallocate report success while leaving holes unallocated, silently breaking the allocation guarantee applications rely on.
A:H - The out-of-bounds read walks potentially gigabytes past the allocation and will fault on unmapped or guard pages, causing a kernel oops/panic, while the inflated length also drives an extremely long 64 KB-at-a-time write loop that stalls the caller.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb/client: handle overlapping allocated ranges in fallocate

smb3_simple_fallocate_range() can skip holes when an allocated range
returned by the server starts before the current fallocate offset. The
skipped hole is not zero-filled, but fallocate still returns success. A
later write to that hole may therefore fail with ENOSPC.

The function queries allocated ranges so that it can preserve existing
contents and write zeroes only into holes. However, the server may return
a range that starts before the current fallocate offset.

For example, assume the fallocate request is [100, 400) and the only
allocated range returned by the server is [0, 200):

        Request:      [100, 400)
        Server range: [  0, 200)  allocated

        Correct:
        [100, 200)    allocated data, skip
        [200, 400)    hole, zero-fill

        Current:
        [100, 300)    skipped
        [300, 400)    zero-filled afterwards

The current code adds the full server range length, 200, to the current
offset 100 and moves to 300. As a result, the hole in [200, 300) is
skipped without being zero-filled.

Fix this by advancing only over the part of the allocated range that
overlaps the current fallocate offset.  Ignore ranges that end before the
current offset and reject ranges whose end offset overflows.

This also prevents a malformed range length from causing an out-of-bounds
zero-buffer read.

A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in SKYSEA Client View and SKYMEC IT Manager. If this vulnerability is exploited, an attacker who can log in to a Windows system on which the affected product is installed may be able to execute arbitrary code on another Windows system that has the affected product installed and can receive UDP packets from that system.

references.name: jackson-dataformats-binary 2.18.10 release notes (maps #725/#726 to CVE IDs)

workarounds.value: No StreamReadConstraints setting mitigates this: maxNameLength is the control that is not enforced, and maxDocumentLength is disabled by default (-1). Bound request body size ahead of the parser, set StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength explicitly on the CBORFactory, and cap JVM heap so a single document cannot exhaust process memory. Avoid parsing untrusted CBOR input where these limits cannot be applied.

supportingMedia.value: No StreamReadConstraints setting mitigates this: maxNameLength is the control that is not enforced, and maxDocumentLength is disabled by default (-1). Bound request body size ahead of the parser, set StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength explicitly on the CBORFactory, and cap JVM heap so a single document cannot exhaust process memory. Avoid parsing untrusted CBOR input where these limits cannot be applied.

descriptions.value: The CBOR parser in FasterXML jackson-dataformats-binary never invokes StreamReadConstraints.validateNameLength() when decoding JSON object property names, so the maxNameLength limit is not enforced for this format. CBORParser._decodeLongerName() decodes a definite-length property name with no length check, and CBORParser._decodeChunkedName() delegates to the value-oriented _finishChunkedText() routine, which validates maxStringLength rather than maxNameLength. An attacker who can have a CBOR document parsed may therefore embed a single property name of unbounded length; the parser buffers the whole name in memory before returning it, whatever maxNameLength is configured to. Because StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength is also disabled by default, nothing else bounds the name under default settings, so the only limits are the attacker's upload capacity and available heap, leading to memory exhaustion and denial of service. No privileges beyond the ability to submit data to a parsing endpoint are required, and exploitation needs only that the bytes reach CBORFactory parsing, directly or through an ObjectMapper configured with the CBOR module. jackson-core's own JSON parsers enforce maxNameLength incrementally during name decoding; this gap is specific to the binary formats. maxNameLength and validateNameLength were introduced in jackson-core 2.16.0, so releases before 2.16.0 do not contain the constraint that is left unenforced. This issue is tracked together with the Smile parser defect in the same vendor advisory, GHSA-3v8f-v6vx-fmrm, which covers both binary formats. The CBOR parser defect (jackson-dataformats-binary issue #725) is CVE-2026-68495; the Smile parser defect (issue #726) is assigned CVE-2026-68496.

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The malformed blob is consumed by request_firmware() from the local firmware search path during tas2781 codec probe (tasdevice_dsp_parser/tas2781_load_calibration); there is no network, adjacent-network, or peer-supplied data path into the parser, so local presence on the affected system is required.
AC:L - Simply omitting the NUL terminator at the end of a coef/cal .bin file makes strlen() run past fmw->size deterministically on every load — no race, no timing window, and no memory-layout precondition the attacker cannot influence.
PR:L - The parsing path contains no capability, credential, or privilege check whatsoever, and the firmware search path on many embedded/Android/appliance deployments lives on a vendor or data partition writable by non-root system accounts; a low-privileged local account is therefore sufficient to be positioned to place the blob.
UI:N - Parsing runs from the asynchronous request_firmware_nowait() completion callback during device probe/bind; once the file is in place it is consumed automatically at the next boot or driver bind with no victim action required.
S:U - The out-of-bounds read occurs in kernel memory belonging to the same kernel that hosts the vulnerable codec driver, with no crossing of a VM, IOMMU, or sandbox boundary.
C:H - strlen() is unbounded — it walks from the description offset through arbitrary kernel memory adjacent to the firmware buffer until a zero byte is found, so the read is not confined to a few bytes and touches heap/vmalloc contents outside the intended allocation.
I:N - The defect is purely a read: the computed length is re-validated against fmw->size afterwards (and int/size_t promotion makes overflowed sums fail the check), so no out-of-bounds write or corrupted parse offset results from the OOB strlen.
A:H - Firmware buffers are vmalloc/kmalloc allocations, so a strlen() walk past the end readily crosses into an unmapped page or guard page and produces a kernel oops/panic, which is High availability impact.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ASoC: tas2781: bound firmware description string parsing

The TAS2781 firmware parser reads several variable-length description
strings with strlen() before checking that the string terminator is
present inside the firmware blob. A malformed firmware image without a
NUL terminator can therefore make the parser walk past the end of the
firmware buffer before the later size checks run.

Add a small bounded string-length helper and use it for all description
fields that are parsed from the firmware buffer. Keep the existing size
checks for the fixed bytes that follow each string.

cna.title: vmxnet3: fix BUG_ON in vmxnet3_get_hdr_len() for Geneve packets

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The bug is triggered purely by a received Geneve-encapsulated packet processed in the vmxnet3 RX completion path (vmxnet3_rq_rx_complete -> vmxnet3_get_hdr_len); any remote host that can deliver such a frame to a VMware guest's vmxnet3 interface reaches the code, with no local access required.
AC:L - The attacker only needs to send Geneve-encapsulated TCP traffic larger than the MTU to the target; the device then sets rcd.v4/v6/tcp from the inner header and the outer UDP protocol (or an outer/inner IP version mismatch) deterministically hits the BUG_ON, with no race or memory-layout dependency.
PR:N - Packet reception and header-length estimation occur in the driver's NAPI RX path before any socket, credential, or authentication check, so an entirely unauthenticated remote sender triggers it.
UI:N - The panic happens during normal NAPI RX processing of an incoming packet; no action by any local user or administrator is needed.
S:U - The BUG_ON crashes the kernel that owns the vmxnet3 interface, and impact stays entirely within that kernel's security authority with no crossing into the hypervisor or another domain.
C:N - The header parsing is bounded by the explicit skb_headlen()/maplen checks, so no out-of-bounds read occurs and no kernel memory contents are disclosed to the attacker before the BUG_ON aborts.
I:N - No out-of-bounds or attacker-controlled write occurs; the mismatch is caught by the BUG_ON assertion, which halts execution rather than corrupting kernel memory or control flow.
A:H - Hitting BUG_ON() in softirq/NAPI context oopses and panics the kernel, taking down the entire guest; a remote attacker can repeat it with a single crafted Geneve packet stream for a persistent denial of service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vmxnet3: fix BUG_ON in vmxnet3_get_hdr_len() for Geneve packets

vmxnet3_get_hdr_len() assumes gdesc->rcd.v4/v6/tcp always describe the
outer header, but for a Geneve-encapsulated packet the device can set
them based on the inner header instead, signalled by the
VMXNET3_RCD_HDR_INNER_SHIFT bit in the completion descriptor. Since the
function never skips the outer encapsulation, this mismatch triggers:

- BUG_ON(hdr.ipv4->protocol != IPPROTO_TCP), because the outer
  protocol is UDP (Geneve), not TCP.
- BUG_ON(hdr.eth->h_proto != ...), when the tunnel's outer and inner
  IP versions differ (e.g. outer IPv6/inner IPv4 or vice versa).

Check VMXNET3_RCD_HDR_INNER_SHIFT up front and bail out, since the
function cannot locate the inner header it would need to parse. Also
convert the remaining BUG_ON()s in this function to return 0
defensively.

cna.title: Bluetooth: RFCOMM: Fix session UAF in set_termios

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: RFCOMM: Fix session UAF in set_termios

rfcomm_tty_set_termios() tests dlc->session without rfcomm_mutex and
later passes the pointer to rfcomm_send_rpn(). The latter dereferences
both session->initiator and session->sock. Meanwhile, krfcommd can
unlink the DLC and free the session while holding rfcomm_mutex.

The race can proceed as follows:

  TTY ioctl task                 krfcommd
  --------------                 --------
  load dlc->session
  enter rfcomm_send_rpn()
                                 lock rfcomm_mutex
                                 clear dlc->session
                                 free session
                                 unlock rfcomm_mutex
  read session->initiator

KASAN reported:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in rfcomm_send_rpn+0x297/0x2a0
  Read of size 4 at addr ffff88810012a850 by task poc/92

  Call Trace:
   rfcomm_send_rpn+0x297/0x2a0
   rfcomm_tty_set_termios+0x50d/0x850
   tty_set_termios+0x596/0x950
   set_termios+0x46a/0x6e0
   tty_mode_ioctl+0x152/0xbd0
   tty_ioctl+0x915/0x1240
   __x64_sys_ioctl+0x134/0x1c0

  Allocated by task 92:
   rfcomm_session_add+0x9e/0x2e0
   rfcomm_dlc_open+0x8b1/0xe00
   rfcomm_dev_activate+0x85/0x1a0
   rfcomm_tty_open+0x90/0x280

  Freed by task 68:
   kfree+0x131/0x3c0
   rfcomm_session_del+0x119/0x180
   rfcomm_run+0x737/0x4710

Add rfcomm_dlc_send_rpn(), which holds rfcomm_mutex while it verifies
that the DLC is still attached and sends the RPN frame. Have the TTY
path use the helper and drop its unlocked session check. This keeps the
session valid through both the frame construction and socket send.

cna.title: wifi: carl9170: fix OOB read from off-by-two in TX status handler

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: carl9170: fix OOB read from off-by-two in TX status handler

The bounds check in carl9170_tx_process_status() uses
`i > ((cmd->hdr.len / 2) + 1)` which is off by two, allowing
2 extra iterations past valid _tx_status entries when the firmware-
controlled hdr.ext exceeds hdr.len/2. Fix by using the correct
comparison `i >= (cmd->hdr.len / 2)`.

cna.title: jackson-databind: unbounded numeric parse in Duration and XMLGregorianCalendar deserialization allows CPU denial of service

timeline.value: CVE ID disclosed publicly in upstream release notes for #6127
GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-q4xh-88c3-wmh7 published by the maintainer

solutions.value: Upgrade to jackson-databind 2.18.10, 2.21.6, 2.22.2 (com.fasterxml.jackson.core) or 3.1.6, 3.2.2 (tools.jackson.core). The fix applies the same validate-length-then-parse idiom already used by NumberDeserializers, calling StreamReadConstraints length validation on the raw string before delegating to DatatypeFactory. The guard deliberately does not extend to javax.xml.namespace.QName, whose local parts may legitimately be long.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to jackson-databind 2.18.10, 2.21.6, 2.22.2 (com.fasterxml.jackson.core) or 3.1.6, 3.2.2 (tools.jackson.core). The fix applies the same validate-length-then-parse idiom already used by NumberDeserializers, calling StreamReadConstraints length validation on the raw string before delegating to DatatypeFactory. The guard deliberately does not extend to javax.xml.namespace.QName, whose local parts may legitimately be long.

references.name: Fix commit (2.x line, forward-merged to the 2.21, 2.22 and 3.x branches)

workarounds.value: Avoid binding javax.xml.datatype.Duration and javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar fields directly from untrusted JSON. Where such fields are required, impose a maximum request body size and a maximum string length at the transport layer, or bind the value as a String, length-check it, and convert it in application code.

supportingMedia.value: Avoid binding javax.xml.datatype.Duration and javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar fields directly from untrusted JSON. Where such fields are required, impose a maximum request body size and a maximum string length at the transport layer, or bind the value as a String, length-check it, and convert it in application code.

descriptions.value: jackson-databind binds a JSON string to a javax.xml.datatype.Duration or javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar field by passing the raw string verbatim to DatatypeFactory.newDuration(value) or newXMLGregorianCalendar(value) in CoreXMLDeserializers.Std._deserialize. These deserializers are registered by default with no opt-in, so a plain ObjectMapper or JsonMapper with no polymorphic typing and no special configuration reaches this path. The XML Schema lexical grammar permits numeric components of arbitrary length, which the JDK materializes through the native BigInteger(String) and BigDecimal(String) constructors, both quadratic in digit count. Because the digits sit inside a JSON string token rather than a JSON number token, jackson-core's StreamReadConstraints.maxNumberLength guard never applies; jackson's own NumberDeserializers call validateIntegerLength or validateFPLength before parsing a stringified number, but the XML datatype deserializer omits that pre-check. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore submit a single request of a few megabytes, such as a Duration value consisting of the letter P followed by several million digits and the letter Y, and force tens of seconds to several minutes of single-threaded CPU work; a handful of concurrent requests can saturate a server's worker threads. This affects com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 2.0.0 before 2.18.10, from 2.19.0 before 2.21.6, and from 2.22.0 before 2.22.2, and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind from 3.0.0 before 3.1.6 and from 3.2.0 before 3.2.2. Users should upgrade to 2.18.10, 2.21.6, 2.22.2, 3.1.6, or 3.2.2.

cna.title: SSH daemon allocates unbounded idle session channels, bypassing max_channels

descriptions.value: CAPEC-125 Flooding

workarounds.value:
No option bounds the number of idle session channels, so the following reduce exposure without eliminating the issue.

* Restrict network access to the SSH daemon to trusted clients. Exploitation requires a successfully authenticated session, so limiting who can authenticate is the most effective control available.
* Set the max_sessions daemon option to a finite value to bound the number of concurrent connections. This limits how many connections can mount the attack in parallel, though a single connection still suffices to exhaust memory.
* Apply operating-system or firewall connection-rate and connection-count limits per source address.
* Monitor node memory externally and restart the emulator when it exceeds a threshold.

Setting max_channels is not a workaround: idle session channels bypass that check entirely.

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Erlang/OTP ssh allows an authenticated remote attacker to exhaust node memory by repeatedly opening session channels that are never assigned a handler.

The "session" clause of ssh_connection:handle_msg/4 checks only minimal_remote_max_packet_size before calling setup_session/5, which unconditionally builds a #channel{} record and stores it in the ETS channel cache. The max_channels daemon option is consulted only by ssh_channel_sup:max_num_channels_not_exceeded/2, which counts supervisor children, so a channel that never gets a shell, exec, or subsystem handler is invisible to the limit and setting the option to a finite value does not mitigate the attack. RFC 4254 section 5.1 permits many session channels per connection, and each record costs only a few hundred bytes, so a single authenticated connection can accumulate channels until the node runs out of memory and the emulator terminates, affecting every application on it. No file contents, credentials, or write access are obtainable.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 18.1.2 before OTP 27.3.4.18, OTP 28.5.0.7, and OTP 29.1.1, corresponding to ssh from 4.1.1 before 5.2.11.13, 5.5.2.6, and 6.0.6. Whether OTP before OTP 18.1.2, corresponding to ssh before 4.1.1, is affected is unknown.

cna.title: drop_monitor: fix size calculations for 64-bit attributes

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The report path runs in net/core/drop_monitor.c whenever a received packet is dropped or hardware-trapped; a remote unauthenticated attacker triggers it simply by sending packets that get dropped, and controls skb->len which feeds payload_len and thus the under-sized allocation.
AC:L - On an affected build the attacker can drive the path at will, tuning packet length byte-by-byte to land the under-budgeted skb exactly at an allocator bucket boundary; no race or unpredictable state is involved.
PR:N - Enabling packet-alert mode is the victim administrator's monitoring configuration; the attacker's own action is only sending packets that get dropped, which needs no account, credentials or privileges on the target.
UI:N - The drop-report path is executed automatically by the kernel workqueue when packets are dropped; no local user action is needed.
S:U - The under-allocated skb and the resulting skb_over_panic() are entirely within the kernel's own security authority; no VM, IOMMU or sandbox boundary is crossed.
C:N - __nla_reserve() detects the overrun in skb_put() and panics before any data is written or read past the buffer, so no memory contents are disclosed to the attacker.
I:N - skb_over_panic() aborts before the out-of-bounds payload copy occurs, so no adjacent memory is modified and no control-flow primitive is obtained.
A:H - The size under-estimation makes skb_put() exceed skb->end, invoking skb_over_panic() which calls BUG() and takes down the machine, a complete and repeatable denial of service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drop_monitor: fix size calculations for 64-bit attributes

net_dm_packet_report_fill() and net_dm_hw_packet_report_fill() use
nla_put_u64_64bit() to append 64-bit attributes (NET_DM_ATTR_PC and
NET_DM_ATTR_TIMESTAMP).

On 32-bit architectures without CONFIG_HAVE_EFFICIENT_UNALIGNED_ACCESS,
nla_put_u64_64bit() may append a 4-byte NET_DM_ATTR_PAD attribute for
64-bit alignment.

However, net_dm_packet_report_size() and net_dm_hw_packet_report_size()
used nla_total_size(sizeof(u64)) instead of nla_total_size_64bit(sizeof(u64)),
budgeting 12 bytes instead of up to 16 bytes.

This under-estimation of SKB size can lead to an skb_over_panic() when
__nla_reserve() or skb_put() is subsequently called.

Fix this by using nla_total_size_64bit(sizeof(u64)) in both size calculations.

cna.title: DiceBear: SVG injection via the unescaped rotate option in @dicebear/core (and fontSize/fontWeight in @dicebear/initials)

descriptions.value: DiceBear is an avatar library for designers and developers. Prior to 9.4.3, @dicebear/core interpolates the rotate option into an SVG transform attribute without XML escaping in addRotate in packages/@dicebear/core/src/utils/svg.ts, while @dicebear/initials similarly emits fontSize and fontWeight without escaping in packages/@dicebear/initials/src/index.ts. Runtime callers can pass strings despite the numeric TypeScript types, break out of the attributes, and inject arbitrary SVG markup. Script can execute in the page origin when the generated avatar is inserted inline or served as image/svg+xml and opened directly, although exploitation requires an application to pass untrusted values into these normally developer-controlled options. This issue is fixed in @dicebear/core and @dicebear/initials version 9.4.3.

cna.title: drm/xe/pt: Reset current_op in xe_pt_update_ops_init()

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The bug is reached through the DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND ioctl on an Intel Xe DRM render node (/dev/dri/renderD*), which requires local access to the device file; there is no remote or adjacent-network path.
AC:L - The overflow needs only one retry of the xe_validation_guard()/drm_exec_until_all_locked() loop, and the attacker drives both retry sources itself: concurrent vm_bind/exec threads on the same BOs force drm_exec_retry_on_contention(), and filling VRAM forces xe_validation_retry_on_oom(). Both sides of the race are attacker-controlled and the sequence is repeatable at will.
PR:L - Only an open file descriptor on the Xe render node plus a VM created via DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE is needed; no capability check exists on the vm_bind path. Render nodes are routinely accessible to unprivileged users, Android apps, containers and GPU-sharing tenants.
UI:N - The attacker performs the entire sequence (vm create, bo create, vm_bind with induced contention/memory pressure) from its own process; no victim action is required.
S:U - The out-of-bounds write and the subsequent corrupted-pointer use occur in kernel heap memory within the same security authority as the kernel itself; no VM, IOMMU or sandbox boundary is crossed by the flaw itself.
C:H - After the index inflates, xe_pt_update_ops_fini()/xe_pt_update_ops_abort() iterate i < current_op and read adjacent-slab contents as xe_vma/pt pointers and num_entries, and xe_migrate_update_pgtables_cpu() consumes the corrupted pt_op, giving out-of-bounds reads of kernel objects and a UAF that can be groomed into an arbitrary-read primitive.
I:H - Each retry writes a full struct xe_vm_pgtable_update_op (pointer-rich entries[] plus vma pointer and flags) past the end of the kmalloc'd ops array, with attacker-chosen overflow length and slab size, and the corrupted entries are later fed to xe_pt_free_bind()/xe_pt_abort_bind() and GPU page-table programming — a controllable heap corruption suitable for privilege escalation.
A:H - The commit documents an out-of-bounds write into SLUB-poisoned memory followed by a UAF crash in xe_migrate_update_pgtables_cpu(); an unprivileged process can reliably and repeatedly panic the kernel, and corrupted page-table state additionally wedges the GPU.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/xe/pt: Reset current_op in xe_pt_update_ops_init()

xe_pt_update_ops_init() fails to reset current_op to 0. On the
vm_bind path, ops_execute() calls xe_pt_update_ops_prepare() inside
the xe_validation_guard() / drm_exec_until_all_locked() loop. When
that loop retries due to lock contention or OOM eviction
(drm_exec_retry_on_contention() / xe_validation_retry_on_oom()),
xe_pt_update_ops_prepare() runs again on the same vops, and each
call to bind_op_prepare() increments current_op without resetting it.

After N retries current_op exceeds the array size allocated by
xe_vma_ops_alloc(), causing an out-of-bounds write into
SLUB-poisoned memory and a subsequent UAF crash in
xe_migrate_update_pgtables_cpu() when reading the corrupted pt_op->bind.

Also reset needs_svm_lock and needs_invalidation which are derived in
the same prepare pass and would otherwise cause wrong migrate ops
selection and redundant TLB invalidation on retry.

Fix this by resetting current_op, needs_svm_lock and needs_invalidation
in xe_pt_update_ops_init().

scenarios.value:
AV:A - The attacker must be a node on the same InfiniBand fabric, sending unsolicited GSI (QP1) management datagrams to the victim port; MAD/SA traffic is subnet-local, matching the CVSS "shared physical or logical network" definition rather than routable network reach.
AC:L - No race or unusual precondition is needed: the attacker just sends active RMPP DATA response MADs whose high TID bits name a kernel RMPP agent, and hi_tid is a small cyclic xarray index in [0,2^24) that is trivially enumerated or brute-forced.
PR:N - The MAD receive path accepts unsolicited datagrams from any fabric peer with no authentication; the only gate is ib_mad_enforce_security() P_Key membership, which the default partition typically grants to every node on the subnet.
UI:N - Reassembly state is created entirely from attacker-sent packets in the completion handler; no action by a local user or administrator is needed, and the always-registered ib_sa kernel agent is the target.
S:U - The injected RMPP state, allocations and AH objects all live inside the kernel's own IB MAD layer on the same host, so the impact stays within a single security authority.
C:N - The flaw creates unmatched reassembly state; it provides no out-of-bounds read, no kernel memory disclosure, and the ACKs the kernel emits echo only attacker-supplied header fields.
I:L - An unauthenticated fabric peer can insert arbitrary unsolicited entries into the kernel agent's RMPP reassembly lists and make the kernel emit ACKs, and a colliding entry (SA TIDs come from a predictable tid++ counter) diverts and drops a legitimate SA response's segments — limited, bounded modification of kernel protocol state.
A:H - Each unmatched segment allocates a mad_rmpp_recv, an AH and a retained ~1-2 KB MAD buffer held for 40 seconds with no matching request, so a burst causes unbounded memory/resource exhaustion, while the O(N) rmpp_list walks under an IRQ-disabled spinlock stall MAD processing and break SA/path resolution for the node.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

IB/mad: Drop unmatched RMPP responses before reassembly

Kernel-handled RMPP receive processing starts reassembly for active
DATA responses before the response is matched to an outstanding send.
The normal match happens later, after ib_process_rmpp_recv_wc() has
either assembled a complete message or consumed the segment.

That ordering lets an unsolicited response that routes to a kernel
RMPP agent by the high TID bits allocate or extend RMPP receive state
before the full TID and source address are checked against a real
request. A reordered burst can therefore reach the receive-side
insertion path even though the response would not match any send.

For kernel-handled RMPP DATA responses, require the existing
ib_find_send_mad() match before entering RMPP reassembly. The matcher
already checks the full TID, management class and source address/GID
against the agent wait, backlog and in-flight send lists. If there is
no match, drop the response without creating RMPP state.

This leaves the RMPP window behavior unchanged and only rejects
responses that have no corresponding request.

cna.title: OpenEXR: Heap buffer overflow in PyOpenEXR from literal/prefixed RGB channel name collision

descriptions.value: OpenEXR is the reference implementation and specification for the EXR image format, widely used in the motion picture industry. Versions 3.3.0 through 3.3.12 and 3.4.0 through 3.4.13 contain a heap buffer overflow in PyOpenEXR triggered by a channel-name key collision between literal and prefixed RGB channels. When separate_channels=false, PyOpenEXR maps each physical channel name through channelNameToRGBA() and coalesces the results into a shared RGB array. A crafted flat scanline EXR that contains both a literal channel such as left and prefixed channels such as left.R, left.G, and left.B causes these names to collide, so the wrapper reuses an undersized two-dimensional NumPy array for the coalesced RGB slices and writes out of bounds when OpenEXR.File(path) decodes the pixels. This issue is fixed in versions 3.3.13 and 3.4.14.
