cna.title: Plane: Unauthenticated ORM field-name injection via `group_by`/`sub_group_by` on public deploy boards (DoS + blind oracle)

descriptions.value: Plane is an open-source project management tool. Prior to 1.4.0, the unauthenticated public issues endpoint accepts group_by and sub_group_by query parameters and passes them without an allowlist to grouped paginators, where they are used as ORM field names by F(field), .values(field), .order_by(field), and Window partition_by operations. An anonymous attacker can supply arbitrary field paths that trigger an unhandled FieldError or KeyError and an HTTP 500 response, or force the ORM to resolve __-separated relational paths as a blind traversal oracle. This is the same field-name injection class addressed by earlier order_by sanitization, but that remediation left group_by and sub_group_by unvalidated. The issue does not directly disclose column values because issue_group_values() returns an empty list for unknown fields, the result projection uses a fixed required_fields list, and the subgrouped path raises KeyError before serialization. This issue is fixed in 1.4.0.

A remote peer can return real far-ahead hashes to a syncing node so that honest peers get banned, eroding its peer set and raising eclipse risk.

cna.title: Multiple @opentelemetry/instrumentation-* packages expose database username via unconditional db.user span attribute

descriptions.value: OpenTelemetry JavaScript Contrib provides instrumentation libraries for collecting telemetry from JavaScript applications. Prior to versions 0.66.0 of @opentelemetry/instrumentation-cassandra-driver, 0.65.0 of @opentelemetry/instrumentation-knex, 0.67.0 of @opentelemetry/instrumentation-mongoose, @opentelemetry/instrumentation-mysql, and @opentelemetry/instrumentation-mysql2, 0.46.0 of @opentelemetry/instrumentation-oracledb, 0.73.0 of @opentelemetry/instrumentation-pg, and 0.40.0 of @opentelemetry/instrumentation-tedious, the packages add the database connection username to every instrumented database operation as the db.user span attribute. The attribute is emitted by default and is not controlled by enhancedDatabaseReporting or another opt-in setting. Configured observability backends therefore receive database account names that may expose service topology, role or environment information, and account naming patterns. This issue is fixed in versions 0.66.0, 0.65.0, 0.67.0, 0.46.0, 0.73.0, and 0.40.0 of the respective packages.

cna.title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.6, which verifies DANE-TA as well as DANE-EE records and requires TLS to a host whose validated TLSA records are all unusable. Until then, an SMTP route for each recipient domain concerned that names its mail exchangers with the connection security 'STARTTLS (required)' prevents delivery in cleartext to that domain.

descriptions.value: Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.5 does not enforce TLS for outbound SMTP delivery to a mail exchanger whose DNSSEC-validated TLSA records contain no DANE-EE (usage 3) record, contrary to RFC 7672 section 2.2. The server used only DANE-EE records and treated a validated TLSA record set consisting of DANE-TA (usage 2) or otherwise unusable records as if no records were published, so delivery to such a host fell back to opportunistic TLS. An attacker with an active position on the network path between the server and the recipient's mail exchanger can suppress or break the STARTTLS negotiation and cause messages to be delivered in cleartext, where they can be read and modified.

cna.title: Fabio: Access-control bypass through unnormalized request paths

descriptions.description: CWE-41: Improper Resolution of Path Equivalence
CWE-289: Authentication Bypass by Alternate Name

descriptions.value: Fabio is an HTTP(S) and TCP router for deploying applications managed by consul. Prior to 1.7.3, route/table.go selects targets using raw req.URL.Path, while proxy/http_proxy.go applies per-route ACL and basic-auth checks to the selected target and forwards the raw path to the origin. Dot-segment, encoded-dot, or repeated-slash variants can fall through to a less restrictive route that reaches the same backend; the backend then normalizes the path and serves the protected resource without the configured access controls. A less restrictive fallback route must reach the same backend; without one, the request returns 404. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.3.

affected.product: Export and Import Users and Customers

descriptions.value: The Export and Import Users and Customers plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.5 via the plugin's own export and re-import workflow. The vulnerability exists because of a CSV escape-character mismatch between the exporter and the importer: class-csvwriter.php writes cells with fputcsv() using PHP's default backslash (\) escape character, while class-csvreader.php parses the same file with fgetcsv() using a double-quote (") as the escape character. As a result, a crafted value stored in a Subscriber's Biographical Info field — containing a backslash-quote sequence followed by a newline — is written as a single quoted CSV field but parsed back as two separate rows on import. The injected second row is then processed by hf_create_customer() as a new user record whose user_login, user_pass, user_email, and role are entirely attacker-controlled, allowing the creation of an arbitrary Administrator account. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Subscriber-level access and above to escalate their privileges to Administrator.

cna.title: DragonflyDB stream RDB deserialization double-free

descriptions.value: Dragonfly is an in-memory data store built for modern application workloads. Prior to 1.40, OpaqueObjLoader::CreateStream in src/server/rdb_load.cc can associate one streamNACK with a consumer group's global PEL and a consumer-local PEL, then free the shared object when a duplicate consumer entry is rejected. Cleanup subsequently frees the same object again. In the default configuration, where Dragonfly ships with authentication disabled, an unauthenticated client can trigger the double-free by sending a crafted serialized stream to RESTORE, causing allocator corruption, denial of service, and potentially attacker-controlled code execution as the Dragonfly service account. The source fix has not yet been mapped to a published release.

cna.title: Sssd: sssd: denial of service via packet length underflow in autofs responder

credits.value: This issue was discovered by Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat.

workarounds.value:
If SSSD automount map integration is not required, disable the autofs responder. Stop and mask the socket-activated service:

# systemctl stop sssd-autofs.socket sssd-autofs.service
# systemctl mask sssd-autofs.socket

If 'autofs' is explicitly listed in the services directive under the [sssd] section of /etc/sssd/sssd.conf, remove it and restart the SSSD service:

# systemctl restart sssd

If autofs support is required, restrict access to the autofs responder UNIX socket (typically /var/lib/sss/pipes/autofs) to trusted local users. Note that disabling the autofs responder prevents SSSD from resolving automount maps, and restarting SSSD may temporarily disrupt identity lookups and active automount operations.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in SSSD. A local attacker can exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted request with an invalid packet length to the autofs responder UNIX socket. This causes an integer underflow and an out-of-bounds memory read, which can crash the responder process and result in a denial of service (DoS).

cna.title: Nx daemon and plugin worker sockets are accessible to other local users

descriptions.value: Nx is a monorepo solution for TypeScript and polyglot codebases. From 14.6.0 until 22.7.9 and 23.1.2, Nx creates Unix domain sockets for its daemon and isolated plugin workers in shared temporary locations without owner-only directory and socket permissions. Another unprivileged local account on a shared build server, developer host, or multi-user container can discover and connect to a running socket because the transport performs no authentication and relies on filesystem containment. The daemon's PROCESS_IN_BACKGROUND request accepts a module path and invokes its default export, allowing a caller that controls a file to execute code as the account running Nx; other handlers can expose workspace file contents, project graphs, and task hashes. Disabling the daemon alone does not remove the vulnerable plugin-worker sockets, while single-user machines without another local account are not exposed. This issue is fixed in versions 22.7.9 and 23.1.2.

cna.title: Apache Struts: Disproportionate response size when rendering BigDecimal request parameters

descriptions.value:
Asymmetric resource consumption (amplification) vulnerability in Apache Struts. When a request parameter is bound to an arbitrary-precision decimal (java.math.BigDecimal) property that is then rendered through the Struts tag library, the framework can produce a response many orders of magnitude larger than the request, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust server CPU and outbound network capacity with sustained low-volume traffic. Applications that do not bind request parameters to BigDecimal properties, or never render such a property through the Struts tag library, are not affected.

This issue affects Apache Struts: from 2.5.14 through 2.5.33, from 6.0.0 through 6.11.0, from 7.0.0 through 7.3.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.12.0 or 7.4.0, which fixes the issue.

x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix ensures that correlation-based lookups are authorized against the live event and attribute access control lists rather than the stale distribution snapshot on the correlation row. A new filtering step validates related event IDs against the current event ACL before returning them, and attribute queries for non-admin users now include the live ACL conditions. Additionally, Event and Object fields are stripped from returned attribute results to prevent incidental metadata leakage.
assumptions: The affected version boundary (< 2.5.48) is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48, 38 commits after fix); the exact first affected version is not stated in the patch.
CVSS PR:L assumes the attacker needs a standard authenticated MISP account with read access to at least one event; no evidence supports a lower or higher privilege requirement.
CAPEC-114 is the closest available pattern; the actual mechanism is a stale authorization snapshot rather than a classic privilege-escalation vector, so the mapping is approximate.

The patch does not specify whether the vulnerability requires the event to have been restricted after correlation creation, or whether other state changes (e.g., sharing group modification) also trigger the issue; the commit message mentions 'restricted' as the primary scenario.
No public exploit or PoC is referenced; exploitation status is assumed to be 'none'.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In DefaultCorrelationBehavior.php: (1) runGetRelatedAttributes now builds query conditions that include the live attribute ACL (buildConditions) for non-site-admin users, and ensures Event and Object are contained in the query for proper filtering; (2) after fetching related attributes, Event and Object sub-objects are unset from each result; (3) fetchRelatedEventIds now passes its results through a new __filterVisibleEventIds method that queries the Event model with createEventConditions to verify each event ID is still visible to the user; (4) the new __filterVisibleEventIds method returns the event IDs unchanged for site admins or empty lists, otherwise filters against the live event ACL.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: Network vector: MISP is a web application accessible over the network. Low complexity: the attacker simply performs a normal attribute search that triggers correlations; no race condition or special setup is needed. No attack requirements: the stale correlation row exists naturally after any event restriction. Low privileges: the attacker needs an authenticated account with read access to at least one event. No user interaction: the attacker initiates the search themselves. High vulnerability-component confidentiality impact: full attribute values and event metadata of restricted events are exposed. No integrity or availability impact on the vulnerable or subsequent components.

capecRationale.rationale: The authorization state used for correlation lookups was incorrectly adjusted (stale) relative to the actual event ACL. An attacker with a legitimate account could exploit this misalignment to access data beyond their intended privilege scope. This is the closest CAPEC pattern; the exact mechanism is a stale authorization snapshot rather than a classic privilege-escalation primitive, so the mapping is approximate.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The correlation lookup path failed to enforce the current (live) authorization state of the target events and attributes. Access was granted based on a stale snapshot rather than the actual ACL, effectively missing the authorization check for restricted events.

The access control decision relied on outdated data (the distribution columns copied onto the correlation row) that did not reflect the current published/sharing-group state of the event, leading to improper access control.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains an authorization flaw in its correlation handling during attribute searches. When a user performs an attribute search that triggers correlation lookups, the system authorized access to correlated attributes and events based on a stale distribution snapshot stored on the correlation row rather than the live event access control list.

Because the correlation row's distribution columns are a point-in-time copy that lacks a published flag, the authorization check becomes incorrect when an event is subsequently restricted (for example, its sharing group is changed or it is unpublished). As a result, an authenticated user could retrieve attributes and event details belonging to events they no longer have permission to view.

Preconditions:

- An authenticated user with at least read access to some events in the instance.

- The existence of correlations between events, at least one of which has been restricted after the correlation was created.

Impact:

- Confidentiality: exposure of attribute values and event metadata that the user is not authorized to access.

Affected versions: MISP prior to v2.5.48.

cna.title: react/http: Unbounded HTTP Client Response Header Buffering Leads to Memory Exhaustion DoS

descriptions.value:
react/http is an event-driven, streaming HTTP client and server implementation for ReactPHP. From 1.0.0 until 1.11.1, React\Http\Browser uses ClientRequestStream::handleData() to append response-header bytes to an internal buffer without enforcing a size limit. A remote server can send a valid status line and partial header, withhold the 

 or 

 header terminator, and continue streaming data so the buffer grows for the life of the connection. Applications that fetch attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced URLs, including URLs reached through redirects, can exhaust PHP memory_limit and crash the event-loop or worker process. Confidentiality and integrity are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.1.

descriptions.description: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

cna.title: Apache Struts: Shared message formatter exposes date and time values across concurrent requests

descriptions.value:
Concurrent execution using shared resource with improper synchronization ('race condition') vulnerability in Apache Struts. Where a localized message formats a date or time argument, the formatter retained for that message by the application-wide text provider is used by concurrently served requests without isolation, so a value belonging to one user can appear in another user's response, or the rendering can fail and surface as a server error. Applications whose localized messages format no date or time arguments are not affected.

This issue affects Apache Struts: from 2.0.0 through 2.3.37, from 2.5.0 through 2.5.33, from 6.0.0 through 6.11.0, from 7.0.0 through 7.3.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.12.0 or 7.4.0, which fixes the issue.

assumptions: The tag_version_boundary (v2.5.48, 50 commits after fix) is used as an approximate upper bound for affected versions; exact version boundaries are not explicitly stated in the patch metadata.

PR:L assumes the attacker needs only a basic authenticated MISP account with access to at least one event; higher-privilege roles may be required depending on deployment configuration, but the patch does not specify this.

VC:L assumes the disclosed metadata (event titles, dates, correlation counts) constitutes a low confidentiality impact; in highly sensitive threat-intelligence environments the impact could be rated higher.
CAPEC-126 is the closest available mapping; no CAPEC precisely describes authorization bypass via a stale snapshot in a correlation/join table.
The 'published' flag and distribution/sharing group checks are assumed to be the primary authorization mechanisms in MISP's event model, based on the commit message and patch context.
No public exploit or active exploitation is assumed; the patch does not reference any CVE, advisory, or exploitation evidence.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In EventsController.php (viewRelatedEvents) and Event.php (getRelatedEvents), the query that fetches related event metadata previously used only Event.id IN (relatedEventIds) as the condition. The patch replaces this with a call to createEventConditions($user), which builds the full set of authorization conditions (published flag, distribution, sharing group), and then adds the Event.id filter on top. The stale comment claiming ACL was enforced via the correlation table was removed. Two files changed, 8 insertions, 9 deletions.

AC:L: An authenticated user simply requests the related events endpoint; no race condition or complex manipulation is needed. AT:N: No attack-target manipulation required. PR:L: Requires a low-privilege authenticated user with access to at least one event. UI:N: No user interaction needed. VC:L: Disclosure is limited to event metadata (title, date, correlation counts), not full event content or attributes. VI:N, VA:N: No integrity or availability impact. capecRationale.rationale: The attacker leverages the trusted correlation relationship stored in the correlation table. The system treated the correlation entry as a sufficient authorization basis, but the snapshot data was stale and incomplete (missing published flag), allowing access to event metadata the caller should not see. This is the closest CAPEC to the pattern of relying on a trusted data source that does not reflect current authorization state. Uncertainty: no CAPEC perfectly describes 'stale authorization snapshot in a join table'; CAPEC-126 is the best available match.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The related events query did not apply the caller's per-event authorization checks (published status, distribution, sharing group). The system relied on a stale snapshot in the correlation table instead of re-validating access, effectively omitting the authorization step for the returned events.

Even though some authorization existed (via the correlation table snapshot), it was based on outdated data and lacked the published flag check, making the authorization decision incorrect for events whose access parameters had changed or that were unpublished.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains an authorization bypass in the related events listing functionality. When a user requests the list of events correlated to a given event, the system retrieved related event metadata directly from the correlation table without re-validating the caller's access rights against each related event.

The correlation table stores a snapshot of the event's distribution level and sharing group at the time the correlation was created, and does not carry the published flag. As a result, events that the caller is not permitted to open—because they are unpublished, or because their distribution or sharing group has changed since the correlation was recorded—were still returned with their metadata (title, date, correlating value counts).

Preconditions:

- An authenticated user with access to at least one event in MISP.

- The existence of correlation entries linking that event to other events the user should not be able to view.

Impact:

- Unauthorized disclosure of event metadata (titles, dates, correlation counts) for events the user has no right to access.

- Potential reconnaissance of threat-intelligence event names and timelines across sharing groups.

Affected: MISP versions prior to the fix commit (2ffa97f05).

descriptions.value: A NULL pointer dereference in the illumos Network Auto-Magic daemon (nwamd) allows a local user to crash the daemon. nwamd_door_switch() in usr/src/cmd/cmd-inet/lib/nwamd/door_if.c writes to the caller's request structure before checking that a request was supplied, and before checking the caller's credentials. Because the nwamd door at /etc/svc/volatile/nwam/nwam_door is accessible to all local users, an unprivileged user can issue a door_call() with no argument data to crash nwamd; repeated calls place the svc:/network/physical:nwam service into maintenance, stopping automatic network configuration. nwamd runs only when svc:/network/physical:nwam is enabled, which is not the default. cna.title: Code execution through Java method calls in HSQLDB databases

credits.value: Thomas Rinsma and Edoardo Geraci from Codean Labs
Minseong Kim of NSHC Red Alert Labs

descriptions.value: CAPEC-35 Leverage Executable Code in Non-Executable Files

LibreOffice bundles the HSQLDB database engine, which can be used through the generic JDBC database driver as well as through the support for embedded databases. HSQLDB lets SQL statements call Java methods, limited to the classes that are permitted. When HSQLDB was used through the generic JDBC driver this limit did not apply, so SQL in a crafted document could call any Java method and run code. In fixed versions SQL can call only the built-in functions of HSQLDB, whichever way the database is reached.

cna.title: GraphQL Tools has prototype pollution in well-established utility function `mergeDeep`

descriptions.value: GraphQL Tools provides utilities for building, stitching, and mocking GraphQL schemas. Prior to 12.0.1, the GraphQL Tools utils package's mergeDeep function follows inherited properties while recursively merging source objects and does not exclude __proto__, constructor, or prototype keys. An unauthenticated GraphQL client can alias fields to those names so responses from two subgraphs collide during ordinary supergraph result merging, causing mergeDeep to traverse Object and Function prototypes and overwrite Function.prototype.call with a subgraph-supplied value. cna.title: Teable: Arbitrary root file write via attachment presign hash path traversal

descriptions.value: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.

descriptions.value: Path Traversal (CWE-22) in the execute_obj function of the archive object viewer (peach.pas) in PeaZip 11.2.0 and earlier on Windows allows an attacker who convinces a victim to preview an entry of a crafted archive via the "Preview with... -> Associated application" action (Shift+Ctrl+O) to execute an arbitrary program already present on the victim's system, with no warning dialog. The function validates only outname (PeaZip's own temporary directory) with checkfiledirname, while the string actually executed is the concatenation outname+tempstring; tempstring is taken verbatim from the archive entry name (StringGridList.Cells[12,...]) and is never validated. checkfiledirname (list_utils.pas) rejects control and reserved characters in the file name but performs no ".." path-containment check, so an entry named ../../../../Windows/System32/calc.exe escapes the extraction directory and is passed to cp_open -> ShellExecuteW; the extracting backend (7-Zip) strips the traversal while the opener does not. In addition, the SECEXTCONST dangerous-extension confirmation prompt is implemented only in the double-click handler (grid_obj_open) and not on this preview route, so an executable inside an archive reaches ShellExecuteW unannounced, and where the prompt does fire it names the entry's display name rather than the resolved path that will run. Arbitrary code execution was demonstrated with a proof of concept against official PeaZip builds, confirmed on two archive formats (.zip and .tar) to show the defect is in PeaZip's own path handling and not in a single format parser.

cna.title: Temporal Server applies inbound namespace replication from a connected peer cluster to local namespaces

credits.value: Zellic, who reported this issue responsibly to Temporal Technologies

descriptions.value: Unauthorized modification of namespace metadata on the receiving cluster by a connected replication peer, for local namespaces, which are never replicated to that peer. Demonstrated effects on a local namespace are a change of state to Deprecated, the peer recorded as the namespace's active cluster, retention reduced to one minute, and new Workflow starts in that namespace failing. No confidentiality impact was demonstrated.

solutions.value: Upgrade to Temporal Server 1.30.8, 1.31.4, or 1.32.1, as appropriate for the deployed minor release line, and keep the dynamic configuration setting history.validateReplicationTaskSourceCluster at its default of true. Fixed releases ignore an inbound namespace replication task, including one applied through the namespace metadata refresh that history replication can trigger, when it targets a namespace the receiving cluster stores as local, and ignore inbound task queue user data replication for a local namespace. With history.validateReplicationTaskSourceCluster enabled, fixed releases also ignore an inbound history replication task when the sending cluster is not in the namespace's cluster list, which for a local namespace is every remote cluster. The fix does not change how a connected peer can update a global namespace replicated with the receiving cluster. Fixed releases do not repair a local namespace that was already modified; review local namespaces, including temporal-system, as described in the workarounds. Temporal Server releases up to and including 1.29.7 are outside the supported window and receive no fix; operators on those releases should upgrade to a supported line.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to Temporal Server 1.30.8, 1.31.4, or 1.32.1, as appropriate for the deployed minor release line, and keep the dynamic configuration setting history.validateReplicationTaskSourceCluster at its default of true. The fix does not change how a connected peer can update a global namespace replicated with the receiving cluster. Fixed releases do not repair a local namespace that was already modified; review local namespaces, including temporal-system, as described in the workarounds. Temporal Server releases up to and including 1.29.7 are outside the supported window and receive no fix; operators on those releases should upgrade to a supported line.

references.name: Backport pull request for the 1.32 release line
Backport pull request for the 1.31 release line
Backport pull request for the 1.30 release line

workarounds.value: Until upgrading, register a remote cluster, and keep its connection enabled, only when that cluster and everyone able to control it are trusted with administrative authority over every namespace on the receiving cluster, including its local namespaces and temporal-system. Disabling the connection to a remote cluster stops the receiving cluster from pulling replication tasks from it, and also stops legitimate replication of global namespaces with that cluster. Review local namespaces, including temporal-system, for a cluster list or active cluster other than the current cluster.

supportingMedia.value: Until upgrading, register a remote cluster, and keep its connection enabled, only when that cluster and everyone able to control it are trusted with administrative authority over every namespace on the receiving cluster, including its local namespaces and temporal-system. Disabling the connection to a remote cluster stops the receiving cluster from pulling replication tasks from it, and also stops legitimate replication of global namespaces with that cluster. Review local namespaces, including temporal-system, for a cluster list or active cluster other than the current cluster.

descriptions.value: A connected peer cluster can modify a Temporal Server cluster's local namespaces, which are never replicated to that peer, because the receiving cluster applies inbound namespace replication updates to them. In a multi-cluster deployment, each cluster pulls replication tasks from the remote clusters an administrator has registered with connection enabled; the sending side excludes local namespaces, but the receiving side does not apply the same rule. When an inbound task names an existing namespace, the server checks at most that the namespace identifiers match, then overwrites its state, description, owner, retention, archival settings, and cluster list, and its active cluster when the task carries a higher failover version, without checking that the namespace is global. A party that controls a registered peer's replies, by operating or compromising it, can therefore change any local namespace whose name and identifier it can supply, without any credential on the receiving cluster: for example, marking it Deprecated, making the peer its active cluster, and shortening its retention, after which new Workflow starts in that namespace fail. Local namespaces include the built-in temporal-system namespace. Namespace metadata the History service refreshes from the peer while processing its history replication tasks passes through the same logic. A cluster with no remote cluster registered with connection enabled is not exposed.

When an inbound task names an existing namespace, the server checks at most that the namespace identifiers match, then overwrites its state, description, owner, retention, archival settings, and cluster list, and its active cluster when the task carries a higher failover version, without checking that the namespace is global. A party that controls a registered peer's replies, by operating or compromising it, can therefore change any local namespace whose name and identifier it can supply, without any credential on the receiving cluster: for example, marking it Deprecated, making the peer its active cluster, and shortening its retention, after which new Workflow starts in that namespace fail. Local namespaces include the built-in temporal-system namespace. Namespace metadata the History service refreshes from the peer while processing its history replication tasks passes through the same logic. A cluster with no remote cluster registered with connection enabled is not exposed.

configurations.value: Exploitation requires that the receiving cluster has registered the attacker's cluster as a remote cluster with connection enabled, which in turn requires clusterMetadata.enableGlobalNamespace to be true, and that the attacker controls the replication task replies that cluster returns. The attacker needs no credential on the receiving cluster, because the receiving cluster initiates the connection and authenticates the peer. The privileges-required assessment treats control of a registered peer as a high privilege: a registered peer is already trusted to change the metadata of every global namespace replicated with it, including failing it over, and this issue extends that authority to the receiving cluster's local namespaces, which the peer was never granted. The attacker must supply the target namespace's name and identifier. A local namespace's identifier is never sent to the peer by replication, but the identifier is not a secret and is returned to any caller that can describe the namespace, and temporal-system has the same identifier in every deployment, so this is not scored as an attack complexity factor. Releases before 1.17.0 do not compare the identifier on the update path at all, so there the namespace name alone is sufficient.

cna.title: ModSecurity: RFC 2231 `filename*` Parameter Bypasses Multipart Filename Rules on RFC-Compliant Backends (Go, Python, Node, Java)

descriptions.value: ModSecurity is an open source, cross platform web application firewall (WAF) engine for Apache, IIS and Nginx. From 3.0.0 until 3.0.17, ModSecurity's multipart parser does not apply the RFC 2231 filename* parameter precedence used by common Go, Python, Node.js, and Java application parsers. A Content-Disposition header can provide a benign filename parameter for ModSecurity and a different encoded filename* value that the backend prefers, causing MULTIPART_FILENAME rules and the application to make security decisions on different names. Applications that use the backend-selected name for storage, extension checks, or content-type inference can therefore receive a filename that bypassed WAF inspection. PHP's native multipart parser is not affected by this discrepancy. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.17.

cna.title: stream-json: Prototype pollution: Assembler writes this.current[this.key] on plain objects

descriptions.value: stream-json is a micro-library of stream components for processing JSON and JSONC with a minimal memory footprint. Prior to 3.6.0, Assembler materializes object properties with plain assignment, so an input key named __proto__ invokes the inherited setter and causes parsed object prototype replacement instead of creating an own data property. Applications that make authorization or feature decisions from inherited values can therefore consume attacker-controlled properties, and a null prototype can disrupt code that expects Object.prototype methods. The researcher treats parsing untrusted JSON as part of the project contract, while the maintainer states that documented inputs are locally owned dumps, exports, or logs and characterizes the attack vector as local. The global Object.prototype is not polluted. This issue is fixed in version 3.6.0.

cna.title: LifterLMS <= 10.2.1 - Authenticated (Custom+) PHP Object Injection via 'custom' Lesson Data

affected.product: LifterLMS – WP LMS for eLearning, Online Courses, & Quizzes

descriptions.value: The LifterLMS – WP LMS for eLearning, Online Courses, & Quizzes plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 10.2.1 via deserialization of untrusted input . This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present. This vulnerability is only exploitable during lesson creation when a temporary lesson ID triggers the custom metadata path, and requires the attacker to hold a role with the edit_course capability, such as Instructor, Instructor's Assistant, LMS Manager, or Administrator.

cna.title: ZoneMinder failed token handling bypasses web authentication

descriptions.value: ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application. In versions 1.34.0 through 1.36.38, the web interface mishandles failed token authentication in web/includes/auth.php. validateToken() returns false when a token is malformed or has an invalid signature, but the caller assigns that value to the global $user variable; because web/index.php tests isset($user), boolean false is treated as a present user and the normal login redirect is skipped. This can dispatch views that rely on the outer authentication gate, including the zones view, which accepts an attacker-selected monitor ID and discloses monitor and zone metadata without an independent permission check. Permission helpers receive the false user value and deny privileged operations, so unauthorized state changes have not been established. This vulnerability is fixed in version 1.36.63, where conversion to ZM\User objects causes invalid token state to fail before view dispatch. Later defense-in-depth changes explicitly leave $user unset after failed token validation and reject non-ZM\User values at the web authentication gate.

descriptions.description: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

descriptions.value: The unstructured library provides open-source components for ingesting and pre-processing images and text documents, such as PDFs, HTML, Word docs, and many more. Prior to 0.24.1, partition_html(html_parser_version="v2") and the VLM partitioner can preserve untrusted document tags, attributes, text, and link targets in metadata.text_as_html, while elements_to_html() emits the result as an HTML document. The to_html() path in unstructured/documents/ontology.py does not escape output or reject unsafe URL schemes, allowing event-handler attributes, attribute breakout markup, and javascript: links to survive parsing. When the generated HTML or text_as_html is rendered in a browser, attacker-controlled script can execute in the viewer's origin, including in document-ingestion workflows where a privileged reviewer opens submitted content. This issue is fixed in version 0.24.1.

cna.title: WPCOM Member <= 1.7.27 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via 'uuid' and 'code' Parameters on Social-Login Callback

descriptions.value: The WPCOM Member plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.27 via the `uuid` and `code` parameters of the social-login callback handler registered on the `init` hook. The vulnerability exists because the `login` function's social-login flow performs no nonce validation, no OAuth state verification, and no per-visitor namespace isolation in the session store, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to issue a crafted GET request that writes an attacker-named, attacker-valued entry into the global session namespace (bypassing the per-visitor prefix by prepending an underscore), then issue a second GET request triggering `weapp_new_user()` to read that forged entry and resolve the attacker-supplied `openid` value to a bound WordPress account before `wp_set_auth_cookie()` establishes a fully authenticated session. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any WordPress user — including administrators — whose bound social provider identifier (openid/unionid) is known or discoverable. Successful exploitation requires that the target site has at least one social provider configured (which activates the vulnerable handler) and that the attacker knows or can enumerate the victim account's bound openid or unionid.

descriptions.value: copyparty is a portable file server. Prior to 1.20.19, FTP upload path handling does not confine destinations to configured copyparty volumes. When FTP or FTPS is explicitly enabled, a low-privileged authenticated user can submit traversal paths during upload to create a new file outside configured volumes wherever the copyparty process has write permission. The attacker cannot read or overwrite files, the output name receives a randomized suffix, and copyparty does not execute the file; however, unrelated software on the same host could process the newly created file. cna.title: OWASP Coraza WAF: jsDecode Off-by-One in Octal Escape Handling Enables WAF Bypass

descriptions.value: OWASP Coraza WAF is a golang modsecurity compatible web application firewall library. From 3.0.0 until 3.8.0, the t:jsDecode transformation in internal/transformations/js_decode.go:64-70 includes the backslash in the octal buffer, causing ParseInt to fail and return a null byte. The flaw is triggered when a rule relies on t:jsDecode and the request contains JavaScript octal escape sequences. An unauthenticated attacker can encode attack syntax with JavaScript octal escapes so the backend decodes the intended bytes while Coraza rules using t:jsDecode inspect corrupted null-byte output. The mismatch can bypass WAF rules and expose the protected application to attacks such as cross-site scripting or SQL injection. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.0.

affected.product: Online Scheduling and Appointment Booking System – Bookly

descriptions.value: The Online Scheduling and Appointment Booking System – Bookly plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 28.4 via the 'id, wp_user_id' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite the WordPress account binding of any Bookly staff record, including those owned by administrators, effectively hijacking a higher-privileged staff member's account association and escalating privileges. Exploitation requires the attacking user to be linked to at least one Bookly staff record, which occurs by default whenever an admin enables the bookly_gen_allow_staff_edit_profile option (active on fresh installs) and links a WordPress user to a staff entry.

cna.title: Simple Shopping Cart < 5.2.6 - Admin+ Stored XSS via PayPal API Credentials

descriptions.value: The Simple Shopping Cart WordPress plugin before 5.2.6 does not escape some of its settings field values before outputting them on an admin settings page, allowing high-privilege users such as administrators to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks, which is notably impactful on multisite installations where administrators do not have the unfiltered_html capability.

cna.title: FacturaScripts < 2026.7 PHP Object Injection via WidgetSelect

descriptions.value: FacturaScripts before version 2026.7 contains a PHP object injection vulnerability in WidgetSelect::processFormData() that allows authenticated attackers to trigger unserialize() on raw POST data without an allowed_classes filter for multiple-select fields. Attackers can submit a serialized XLSXWriter object as the field value to invoke its __destruct() method, deleting arbitrary attacker-specified files such as config.php or backup data, resulting in denial of service and potential application reinstall hijack.

WarehousePG (WHPG) 7.2.1 through 7.6.0 is affected by a missing authorization vulnerability (CWE-862) in the built-in function gp_log_backend_memory_contexts(). Any authenticated database role can run this function without a GRANT. It also gets around the superuser restriction that PostgreSQL places on the underlying pg_log_backend_memory_contexts() function. A low-privileged user can force the segment backends of any other session, superuser sessions included, to write their memory context details to the segment server logs, which the attacker cannot read. Those details can include query text from other users' cached plans, and the call can be repeated to generate large amounts of log output. WarehousePG 6.x is not affected.

An attacker with high privileges could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction. Scope is changed.

cna.title: Avada (Fusion) Builder <= 3.16.2 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'tab_index' and 'empty_notice' Shortcode Attributes

descriptions.value: The Avada (Fusion) Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'tab_index, empty_notice' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.16.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. descriptions.value: Plane is an open-source project management tool. cna.title: Plane: InstanceAdminSignUpEndpoint TOCTOU race allows two concurrent unauthenticated callers to both bootstrap as Plane instance admins

descriptions.value: Plane is an open-source project management tool. From 0.13 until 1.4.0, InstanceAdminSignUpEndpoint in apps/api/plane/license/api/views/admin.py:89-117, 173-229 uses InstanceAdmin.objects.first() for the first-admin check and performs account creation without an atomic transaction, row lock, uniqueness guard, or advisory lock. Two concurrent unauthenticated requests with different email addresses can both observe that no instance administrator exists, create separate User and InstanceAdmin rows, and receive sessions with instance-admin authority. This allows an attacker to share unrestricted instance administration with the legitimate operator. This issue is fixed in 1.4.0.

cna.title: VxWorks 7 improper privilege management

descriptions.value: CAPEC-233 Privilege Escalation

An improper privilege management vulnerability (CWE-269) exists in the command shell of Wind River VxWorks 7 when configured to enforce per-user command privileges. Under certain shell operations, a command may be evaluated without the privilege check that is normally applied, allowing an authenticated user with limited privileges to execute commands they are not authorized to run. Successful exploitation can result in privilege escalation, with impact to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the affected device. The issue affects all versions of VxWorks 7 prior to 26.09.  It has been fixed in 26.09.

cna.title: stream-json: JSONC parser and verifier re-scan the whole accumulated comment on every input chunk

descriptions.value: stream-json is a micro-library of stream components for processing JSON and JSONC with a minimal memory footprint. Prior to 3.6.0, the JSONC parser at stream-json/jsonc/parser.js and verifier at stream-json/jsonc/verifier.js restart comment-terminator scanning from the opening slash whenever a block or line comment spans an input chunk, while retaining the accumulated comment buffer. Delivering a large valid comment across many small chunks therefore causes quadratic CPU work and can stall the Node.js event loop. The maintainer characterizes the attack vector as local because the documented JSONC input is locally owned or user-controlled configuration, rather than input intended for the open internet. This JSONC-only scope does not include the plain JSON parser, which advances through and discards consumed string and number data. This issue is fixed in version 3.6.0.

cna.title: Pki-core: dogtag-pki: redhat-pki: pki: est fullcmc authentication bypass allows certificate mis-issuance with arbitrary subject

workarounds.value: Disable basic authentication for all users. This can be done by removing the field "UserPasswords" for the user entries in the EST DS server.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Dogtag PKI (pki-core). The CMCAuthForEST authentication plugin fails open when an EST fullcmc enrollment request is submitted via BasicAuth without an end-user TLS client certificate. The SSL_CLIENT_CERT session attribute retains the EST subsystem's agent certificate, which causes downstream authorization checks to treat the request as agent-privileged. An authenticated EST user can exploit this to obtain CA-signed certificates with arbitrary subject names.

cna.title: Apache Struts: OGNL injection in the legacy RESTful action mapper

descriptions.value:
Improper neutralization of special elements used in an expression language statement ('Expression Language Injection') vulnerability in Apache Struts. If the application is configured to use the legacy RESTful action mapper, a crafted request can inject an OGNL expression that may lead to remote code execution. Struts 7 is affected only when the OGNL allowlist is disabled; it is enabled by default. Applications using the default action mapper, the restful2 mapper, or the Struts REST plugin are not affected.

This issue affects Apache Struts: from 2.0.0 through 2.3.37, from 2.5.0 through 2.5.33, from 6.0.0 through 6.11.0, from 7.0.0 through 7.3.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.12.0 or 7.4.0, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: Seroval: Memory exhaustion via unchecked TypedArray length in JSON deserialization

descriptions.description: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

descriptions.value: Seroval facilitates JS value stringification, including complex structures beyond JSON.stringify capabilities. Prior to 1.6.3, deserializeTypedArray in fromJSON and fromCrossJSON trusts a deserialized source value as an ArrayBuffer and does not bound the serialized element count. An attacker can provide a small untrusted JSON object with a large length value, causing the array-like TypedArray constructor to synchronously allocate the selected number of elements and exhaust CPU or memory while starving the event loop. The offset check does not reject the crafted source because source.byteLength is undefined. DataView reaches a similar unchecked cast but throws rather than allocating, and the issue has no identified confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.3.

cna.title: AdonisJS HTTP Server: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption and Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity

descriptions.value: AdonisJS HTTP Server is a package for handling HTTP requests in the AdonisJS framework. Prior to 8.2.2 and 9.1.1, the regular expression returned by router.matchers.slug() contains adjacent greedy repetitions with overlapping character classes. When an application applies this matcher to an attacker-controlled route parameter, a long slug ending in a character rejected by the final assertion causes quadratic backtracking and excessive CPU use. Route matching occurs before route and group middleware, so authentication or rate-limiting middleware attached to the route may not prevent an unauthenticated request from blocking the Node.js event loop and stopping the worker from serving unrelated requests or health checks. This issue is fixed in versions 8.2.2 and 9.1.1.

cna.title: Sssd: sssd: denial of service via stale connection state reuse in pam gssapi responder

credits.value: This issue was discovered by Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat.

workarounds.value: A workaround is available for this issue. PAM GSSAPI authentication can be disabled in the SSSD configuration: edit /etc/sssd/sssd.conf, and in the [pam] section remove or comment out the pam_gssapi_services option (or set it to an empty value), so that no service is permitted to use GSSAPI authentication through the PAM responder. Then restart the SSSD service (systemctl restart sssd) to apply the change. Note that disabling PAM GSSAPI authentication prevents clients from authenticating to the affected PAM services using Kerberos tickets, requiring them to use alternative authentication methods such as passwords. Restarting the SSSD service also briefly disrupts ongoing authentication requests. Restarting the PAM responder can restore service after a crash, but it does not remove the underlying flaw.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in SSSD. A local user can cause a denial of service (DoS) by disrupting system authentication services. When handling Generic Security Services Application Programming Interface (GSSAPI) authentication in the Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) responder, cached connection state is freed upon completion without clearing the reference pointer. An attacker can exploit this by sending an additional request over the same connection, causing the service to access invalid memory and unexpectedly terminate.

cna.title: FileRise: TOTP codes are not single-use — valid 6-digit code can be replayed within its window (capture-replay)

descriptions.value: FileRise is a self-hosted web-based file manager with multi-file upload, editing, and batch operations. Prior to 3.23.0, FileRise verifies that a TOTP code is valid for the accepted time window but does not record that the same account and time step already succeeded. An attacker who has the target account's valid primary credential and captures a TOTP code after its successful use can replay that code from another pending-login session before the window closes. The issue does not by itself disclose the primary credential or TOTP code. This issue is fixed in version 3.23.0.

cna.title: Redux Framework <= 4.5.16 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'multi_media' Field Array Key

descriptions.value: The Redux Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'multi_media' Field Array Key in all versions due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post sanitization applied at save time operates only on array leaf values, leaving array keys entirely unsanitized; the injected key is then rendered directly into an id="filelist-<KEY>" HTML attribute without esc_attr() in Redux_Multi_Media::render(), allowing attribute breakout.

cna.title: Mobile builder <= 1.4.2 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Privilege Escalation to wcfm-profile-settings REST Route 'key'/'data' Parameters

descriptions.value: The Mobile builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.2 via the `wcfmmp_profile_settings()` REST handler exposed at `POST /mobile-builder/v1/wcfm-profile-settings`. This is due to a PHP loose-comparison logic flaw in the meta key allow-list check — `strpos( $key, 'mobile_builder' ) == 0` evaluates to `true` for any key that does *not* contain the substring `'mobile_builder'` because `strpos()` returns `false` on no match and `false == 0` is `true` in PHP — combined with a `permission_callback` (`user_permissions_check`) that grants access to any authenticated user by only verifying `$user->exists()`. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to pass an unsanitized `data` array via the `key` and `data` parameters directly to `update_user_meta()`, overwriting arbitrary user meta on their own account — including the `wp_capabilities` meta key — to grant themselves Administrator-level privileges.

cna.title: FileRise: Authenticated ZIP extraction follows a pre-existing symlink and deletes files outside the storage root

descriptions.value: FileRise is a self-hosted web-based file manager with multi-file upload, editing, and batch operations. Prior to 3.23.0, FileRise validates archive entry names but extracts them directly into the authorized live destination before validating resolved paths. If that destination already contains a symlink to a directory outside the storage root, an authenticated non-administrator with extract permission who can upload or otherwise place an attacker-controlled ZIP in that folder can place an ordinary archive entry beneath the link. ZipArchive::extractTo() can then overwrite an external file, and post-extraction cleanup can delete that target through the same linked parent, only where the FileRise process has the required filesystem write or removal permission. The advisory does not establish that the attacker can create the prerequisite symlink through FileRise. This issue is fixed in version 3.23.0.

cna.title: WPSyncSheets For Contact Form 7 <= 1.8.0 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection to Remote Code Execution via Untrusted CF7 Submission Field via maybe_unserialize()

affected.product: WPSyncSheets For Contact Form 7 – CF7 Google Sheets Connector & Save to Database

descriptions.value: The WPSyncSheets For Contact Form 7 – CF7 Google Sheets Connector & Save to Database plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.0 via the 'any non-system CF7 field (e.g., your-message)' parameter parameter. This is due to insufficient sanitization of CF7 submission field values before database storage and the absence of an allowed_classes restriction on maybe_unserialize() during admin retrieval. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server. Successful exploitation of the remote code execution gadget chain requires that a Google Sheets access token be configured in the plugin (its primary advertised feature), as this triggers autoloading of the bundled Monolog 2.10.0 library whose classes form the exploitable gadget chain; however, the underlying PHP Object Injection occurs regardless.

cna.title: OpenEMR: Missing authorization on QRDA Category I/III download endpoints

descriptions.value: OpenEMR is a free and open source electronic health records and medical practice management application. Prior to 8.3.0, custom/ajax_download.php, custom/download_qrda.php, custom/export_qrda_xml.php, and custom/qrda_download.php validate CSRF but do not enforce the patients/med ACL used by the canonical CQM report page. The endpoints also accept an unscoped report_id, allowing a low-privilege authenticated user to reach report generation and download logic for other reports. In a clinic with generated CQM reports, this can expose QRDA Category One and Category Three clinical documents for patients in a measure. This issue is fixed in version 8.3.0.

cna.title: Insights-runtime-extractor: insights-runtime-extractor: container escape via privileged binary execution

workarounds.value:
The vulnerability requires a
code fix to implement a complete privilege drop (setting all three UID/GID
fields, clearing all Linux capability sets, and setting `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`)
before executing any fingerprint binary.

descriptions.value:
The insights-runtime-extractor runs as a privileged DaemonSet (`hostPID: true`)
that scans container processes for runtime fingerprinting. When scanning a
container, the coordinator:

1. **fork()s** a child process
2. **setns()** into the target container's PID and mount namespaces
3. **fchdir()** back to an orphaned FD pointing at the extractor's own root
   filesystem (where `/crio.sock` is hostPath-mounted)
4. Calls **only `seteuid(target_uid)`** — changing the effective UID but leaving
   the **real UID and saved-set-UID at 0** and **retaining the permitted
   capability set**
5. The `check_no_privileged_perms()` guard inspects only the Effective capability
   set (so it passes), and is **skipped entirely when the target runs as uid 0**
6. The `VersionExecutable` fingerprint invokes `fpr_kind_executable` with
   `process.command_line[0]` — the target's argv[0], read from
   `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and **fully controlled by the workload**
7. `fpr_kind_executable` calls `exec.Command(executable, "--version").Output()`
   — executing the **workload's own binary** inside the workload's mount
   namespace while **ruid=0 in the host user namespace**

The executed process can call `setuid(0)` to restore full root with
`CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, and inherits the orphaned cwd which resolves into the extractor
container's filesystem containing the host CRI-O socket.

## Affected Code

### 1. Insufficient privilege drop (Rust — extractor coordinator)

**File:** `extractor/src/insights_runtime_extractor.rs`

```rust
// Lines 139-146 — seteuid-only drop, guard skipped for root containers
join_process_namespaces(process.pid)?;
change_dir(current_dir);
switch_user(*process.uid)?;
if *process.uid != 0 {
    perms::check_no_privileged_perms()
        .expect("Must not have privileged permissions to run fingerprints");
}
fingerprint::run_fingerprints(&config, out_dir, &process);
```

```rust
// Lines 182-185 — only effective UID changed; ruid/suid stay 0
fn switch_user(uid: u32) -> Result<(), ScannerError> {
    debug!("... Becoming user: {uid}");
    seteuid(uid.into()).map_err(|e| ScannerError::Errno(e))
}
```

### 2. Execution of untrusted binary (Go — fingerprint)

**File:** `fingerprints/pkg/utils/file.go`

```go
// Lines 75-80 — executes a path taken verbatim from workload's argv[0]
func GetExecutableVersionOutput(executable string) (string, error) {
    out, err := exec.Command(executable, "--version").Output()
    if err != nil {
        return "", err
    }
    return string(out), nil
}
```

### 3. Workload-controlled path forwarded (Rust — version_executable)

**File:** `version_executable.rs`

```rust
// Lines 29-34 — workload-controlled command_line[0] forwarded to fingerprint
return Some(vec![
    fpr_kind_executable,
    out_dir.to_string(),
    String::from(&process.command_line[0]),
    String::from(&version_executable.runtime_kind_name),
]);
```

## Attack Pattern

**Attacker:** Any tenant able to schedule a pod (unprivileged, any namespace)
**Victim:** The node running the insights-runtime-extractor DaemonSet
**Trigger:** Automatic — the DaemonSet scans all container processes on the node

**Attack sequence:**

1. Attacker creates a pod whose process name matches a configured
   versioned-executable pattern (`node`, `python`, `python3`, `MainThread`,
   or contains `java`)
2. The pod's main binary (at the path matching argv[0]) is a malicious
   executable that calls `setuid(0)` to restore root
3. When the insights operator triggers a scan, the DaemonSet forks, enters the
   attacker's mount namespace, and executes the attacker's binary with ruid=0
4. The attacker's code regains full root with `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` in the host user
   namespace
5. The inherited cwd contains the host CRI-O socket → full node compromise

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [security] Escape the value of the count index field

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [security] Escape the value of the count index field
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The vulnerability is remediated by applying HTML entity encoding to the count field value before it is rendered in the view template. This ensures that any HTML or script markup contained in the value from a remote server is neutralized and displayed as inert text rather than being interpreted by the browser.
assumptions: The affected version boundary is inferred from the nearest tag v2.5.48 with 31 commits after the fix; the exact last affected version is not explicitly stated in the patch.
PR:L assumes the attacker needs at least low-privilege access to a linked MISP server to create or modify an event; if no authentication is required on the linked server, PR could be None.
The CAPEC-1 mapping is the closest standard pattern; no CAPEC specifically covers 'XSS via data from a trusted remote server' as a distinct pattern.
The Co-Authored-By line references an AI assistant (Claude Opus 5.5); it is listed as a tool credit rather than a human remediation developer.
The commit date (24 Sep 2026) is in the future relative to typical CVE timelines; this is taken at face value from the patch metadata.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In the CakePHP view template file app/View/Elements/genericElements/IndexTable/Fields/count.ctp, the assignment of $fieldValue was changed from a raw Hash::extract() call to one wrapped in the h() helper function (CakePHP's HTML-encoding utility). This single-line change ensures the extracted value is HTML-entity-encoded before being used in the template output, preventing injection of markup through the event identifier from a linked server.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N - exploitation occurs over the network via a linked MISP server. AC:L - the attacker only needs to craft an event ID with HTML/JS; no race conditions or complex timing. AT:N - the malicious data is stored in the linked server; no active attack is needed at exploitation time. PR:L - the attacker needs low-privilege access to a linked MISP server to create/modify an event. UI:N - the victim only needs to view the remote event preview index page; no special interaction. VC/VI/VA:N - no direct impact on the MISP server's own confidentiality, integrity, or availability. SC:L - XSS allows reading some data (cookies, DOM) in the victim's browser. SI:L - attacker can modify what the victim sees in the browser. SA:N - no impact on security authority of the victim's system.

capecRationale.rationale: The attack pattern involves injecting script or markup into a web page through a data field (event ID from a linked server) that is rendered without encoding. CAPEC-1 is the closest standard mapping for XSS via untrusted data rendered in a browser context. The specific vector here is a linked MISP server supplying crafted data, which is a variant of the general XSS injection pattern. No more specific CAPEC precisely captures the 'trusted remote server as injection vector' nuance, so CAPEC-1 is the best available match.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The patch adds HTML encoding (h() function) to a value that was previously rendered raw in an HTML context. The commit message explicitly states the value was printed raw, allowing markup injection. This is a textbook stored/reflected XSS due to missing output encoding.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the index table rendering of the remote event preview. The count field template escaped the associated link URL but rendered the field value without HTML encoding. An attacker with the ability to create or modify events on a linked (remote) MISP server could craft an event identifier containing HTML or JavaScript markup. When a user on the local MISP instance views the remote event preview index, the unescaped value is rendered directly in the browser, allowing arbitrary script execution in the victim's session.

Preconditions:

- A linked/remote MISP server is configured and connected to the local instance.

- The attacker has sufficient access on the linked server to create or modify an event with a crafted identifier.

- A victim user on the local instance views the remote event preview index page.

Impact:

- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application.

- Potential session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the authenticated user.

Affected versions: <2.5.48.

cna.title: pREST _groupby function-expression SQL injection (incomplete fix of CVE-2025-58450)

descriptions.description: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command

descriptions.value: pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.

cna.title: PictShare < 3.7.1 Sensitive Information Disclosure via info API

descriptions.value: PictShare before 3.7.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain the secret delete_code and uploader metadata by calling the API::info() endpoint which returns the complete raw metadata object without a field whitelist. Attackers can use the publicly visible file hash to retrieve the delete_code via the info API and then invoke the delete API to permanently delete arbitrary files, while also exposing uploader IP, User Agent, remote port, and SHA-1 hash, resulting in loss of content integrity, availability, and uploader privacy.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-63 Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

DigitalCanion has discovered a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability that allows an authenticated malicious user to inject persistent JavaScript or HTML content, resulting in a denial-of-service condition within the web application.




The specific flaw exists within the web portal listening on TCP port 443, under Configuration → Users → Users List. The vulnerability occurs in the “Microsoft Exchange mailbox” field, which fails to properly validate or sanitize user-supplied input before storing and rendering it.




By injecting malicious JavaScript into this field, an attacker can cause the payload to execute whenever the affected user properties are accessed. This can prevent access to the affected user properties and result in a denial-of-service condition within the application's user-management functionality.

cna.title: Gitea OpenID account linking without session binding

references.name: Fix backport to release/v28: go-gitea/gitea pull request #39744

descriptions.value: The Gitea OpenID association callback in the security settings accepted a positive OpenID 2.0 assertion without checking that the signed-in user had started the linking. Because OpenID 2.0 allows unsolicited assertions, an attacker-controlled OpenID provider could attach the attacker's identity to the account of a signed-in victim who opened a crafted link, and the attacker could then sign in as the victim through OpenID login, which does not apply the local TOTP or WebAuthn checks. The callback now requires a time-limited `state` value bound to the user.

cna.title: Sssd: sssd: denial of service via out-of-bounds write in nfs idmap plugin

credits.value: This issue was discovered by Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat.

workarounds.value: Disable the vulnerable memcache lookup path of the SSSD NFS idmap plugin: in the rpc.idmapd configuration, set `memcache = false` for the SSSD plugin (or switch the translation `Method` away from `sss`), and restart the rpc.idmapd service to apply the change. This makes uid/gid name lookups bypass the vulnerable get_user_from_mc() and get_group_from_mc() code paths. Note that with memcache disabled, lookups are served through the SSSD responder instead of the in-memory cache, which may add lookup latency on systems with heavy NFS identity resolution traffic. No released package fix is currently established for this issue, so this configuration change is the recommended interim workaround until a fixed build is available.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in SSSD's NFS idmap plugin. When retrieving cached user or group names, the plugin detects if an entry exceeds the destination buffer size but fails to abort before copying data. A local attacker can trigger this vulnerability by requesting identity lookups that resolve to oversized cached entries, resulting in an out-of-bounds write. This flaw primarily leads to a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the identity mapping service, and may also corrupt adjacent process memory.

cna.title: YesWiki before 4.6.7 SQL Injection via filtertags filterN parameter

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: YesWiki before 4.6.7 SQL Injection via filtertags filterN parameter

descriptions.value: YesWiki before 4.6.7 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the Bazar filtertags action, which wraps unescaped filterN attribute tokens in quotes and concatenates them into a raw tags.value IN (...) clause. Unauthenticated attackers on default installs can save filtertags markup in a page with a trailing-backslash token that breaks quote parity under MySQL backslash escaping. This lets them inject a five-column UNION subquery to read arbitrary table data such as password hashes.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Zebra 4.4.0 Consensus Divergence via V5 SIGHASH_SINGLE Without Output

descriptions.value: Zebra zebrad 4.4.0 and zebra-script 6.0.0 fail to enforce a ZIP-244 consensus rule, accepting V5 transparent inputs signed with SIGHASH_SINGLE that lack a corresponding output. Attackers can broadcast crafted V5 transactions with more inputs than outputs that Zebra accepts but zcashd rejects, causing a network consensus split.

cna.title: jackson-dataformat-smile: unbounded eager byte[] allocation for raw binary in the async parser allows OutOfMemoryError denial of service

descriptions.value: CAPEC-130 Excessive Allocation

timeline.value: GHSA-h3c2-2m49-r49w published by the maintainer in FasterXML/jackson-dataformats-binary

descriptions.value:
The asynchronous Smile parser (NonBlockingByteArrayParser) uses a raw-binary length prefix taken from untrusted input to allocate a byte[] before the body is read, with no upper bound and no overflow check. On the raw-binary marker 0xFD, _decodeVInt() computes (value << 6) + (i & 0x3F) without the (value >>> 25) != 0 overflow guard present in the blocking SmileParser._readUnsignedVInt, and _startRawBinary then allocates the declared length immediately.



A Smile feed of roughly ten bytes can therefore force an eager allocation of approximately 2 GB, producing an OutOfMemoryError on reactive or asynchronous Smile endpoints. A VInt crafted to overflow int yields a negative length and a NegativeArraySizeException, a RuntimeException that is not a JacksonException and so escapes the parser contract. Either outcome crashes the request or processing thread.



This is the same class of issue as CVE-2020-28491 in the CBOR parser of this library, which was fixed with a LONGEST_NON_CHUNKED_BINARY guard; the asynchronous Smile parser never received the equivalent guard. No privileges or user interaction beyond the ability to submit data for parsing are required.

cna.title: Mitel MiVoice Office 400 Music on Hold WAV File Upload Code Execution

descriptions.value: CAPEC-650 — Upload a Web Service with Malicious Content
CAPEC-242 — Code Injection

DigitalCanion SA has discovered a vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of the product. Authentication may be required to exploit this vulnerability.




The specific flaw exists within the Configuration → Services → Music on Hold functionality of the web portal listening on TCP port 443. The application is intended to allow users to upload WAV audio files but fails to properly validate the uploaded file type. An attacker can exploit this behavior to upload a malicious shared object (.so) instead of a WAV file. When the uploaded file is subsequently processed by the affected component, attacker-controlled code is loaded and executed in the context of the affected process. This can result in remote code execution and potentially full compromise of the underlying Linux system.

cna.title: Plane: Cross-workspace association destruction and issue mutation/read via unscoped queries in BulkDeleteIssuesEndpoint and SubIssuesEndpoint

descriptions.value: Plane is an open-source project management tool. Prior to 1.4.0, BulkDeleteIssuesEndpoint and SubIssuesEndpoint in apps/api/plane/app/views/issue/ accept body- or URL-supplied issue IDs and operate on them without checking that the IDs belong to the caller's workspace and project. The permission decorator on each endpoint validates only that the caller is a member or administrator of the workspace and project named in the URL. BulkDeleteIssuesEndpoint can destroy CycleIssue and ModuleIssue associations belonging to foreign issues. SubIssuesEndpoint can re-parent foreign issues under an attacker-selected issue and return the foreign issues' metadata. This issue is fixed in 1.4.0.
